### Listbox

```
import "@kirana-ui/web/listbox"
```

`<kui-listbox>`: `<kui-listbox>` around `kui-part="root"` and an `item` for each `kui-value` (`kui-disabled`, `kui-label`), which may hold an `indicator`, in the page while the item is chosen. Items may be in a `group` with its `group-label`. `value` and `default-value` (with commas between), `multiple`, `disabled`, `loop`, `name`, `form`; it tells `value-change`.

Attributes of the element (each also a property, in camel case):

- `value` (string): The chosen values: none, one, or with `multiple` several.
- `default-value` (string): The values it starts with, when the caller does not hold `value`. Read once.
- `multiple` (boolean): Whether more than one can be chosen: a press then adds or takes away.
- `disabled` (boolean): Disabled: no item can be chosen.
- `loop` (boolean): Whether the arrows go round from the last item to the first. Default: they do not.
- `name` (string): With a name, the chosen values are submitted with the form around the list.
- `form` (string): The id of the form the list belongs to, when it is not inside it.

Events:

- `value-change`: `event.detail.value`, with `event.detail.details`. `preventDefault()` keeps `value` as it was.

Parts (`kui-part`), each with the `kui-` attributes its element is read for:

- `root`
- `item`: `kui-disabled`, `kui-label`, `kui-value`
- `indicator`: `kui-value`
- `group`: `kui-id`
- `group-label`: `kui-id`

Anatomy:

```
<kui-listbox>
  root
    group (optional, repeated)
      item (repeated)
        indicator
      group-label
```

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- root: The list. It is one stop for Tab.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- item: One choice in the list.
    - `data-selected`: Present on a chosen item.
    - `data-highlighted`: Present on the item the keyboard is on.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- itemIndicator: A mark an item shows while it is chosen.
    - `data-selected`: Present on a chosen item.

These parts write no state attribute or CSS variable of their own: `group` and `groupLabel`.

### Menu

```
import "@kirana-ui/web/menu"
```

`<kui-menu>`: `<kui-menu>` around a `kui-part="trigger"` and a `portal` with a `positioner` (its `kui-side` and the like) around the `popup`, which holds its `item`s (`kui-disabled`, `kui-label`, `kui-close-on-select="false"`), `separator`s, `group`s with a `group-label`, `checkbox-item`s (`kui-checked`, `kui-default-checked`; it tells `checked-change`) with a `checkbox-item-indicator`, and a `radio-group` (`kui-value`, `kui-default-value`; it tells `value-change`) of `radio-item`s (`kui-value`) with a `radio-item-indicator`. A `<kui-menu>` inside a menu is its submenu, its trigger an item of the menu; inside a `<kui-menubar>`, one of the bar's. `open`, `default-open`, `disabled`, `loop-focus`, `modal`; it tells `open-change`.

Events:

- `open-change`: `event.detail.open`, with `event.detail.details`. `preventDefault()` keeps `open` as it was.

Parts (`kui-part`), each with the `kui-` attributes its element is read for:

- `positioner`: `kui-align`, `kui-align-offset`, `kui-anchor`, `kui-arrow-padding`, `kui-collision-boundary`, `kui-collision-padding`, `kui-position-method`, `kui-side`, `kui-side-offset`, `kui-sticky`
- `popup`
- `arrow`
- `separator`
- `item`: `kui-close-on-select`, `kui-disabled`, `kui-label`
- `group`: `kui-id`
- `group-label`
- `checkbox-item`
- `checkbox-item-indicator`
- `radio-group`
- `radio-item`: `kui-close-on-select`, `kui-disabled`, `kui-label`, `kui-value`
- `radio-item-indicator`: `kui-value`
- `trigger`

Anatomy:

```
<kui-menu>
  trigger
  portal
    positioner
      popup
        arrow
        group (optional, repeated)
          item (repeated)
          group-label
          checkbox-item (repeated)
            checkbox-item-indicator
          radio-group (repeated)
            radio-item (repeated)
              radio-item-indicator
          <kui-menu> (repeated)
            portal (as above)
            trigger
        separator (repeated)
```

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- trigger: The button that opens the menu, and what it is placed against.
    - `data-popup-open`: Present when the menu is open.
    - `data-pressed`: Present while its popup is open: it stays pressed, as a button held down.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- positioner: Places the menu against its trigger. It carries the geometry.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-side="top | right | bottom | left | inline-start | inline-end"`: The side of the anchor it is on, after any flip. Asked for as `inline-start` or `inline-end`, it says one of those two when it is beside its anchor.
    - `data-align="start | center | end"`: How it is aligned with the anchor.
    - `data-anchor-hidden`: Present while the anchor is out of view: scrolled away, or clipped by a box around it.
    - `--anchor-width`: The anchor's width.
    - `--anchor-height`: The anchor's height.
    - `--available-width`: The width between the anchor and the edge of the viewport.
    - `--available-height`: The height between the anchor and the edge of the viewport.
    - `--transform-origin`: The point of the popup nearest its anchor, to scale from.
    - `--positioner-width`: The popup's width, as its content lays it out: a design gives the positioner `width: var(--positioner-width)` to animate a change of size.
    - `--positioner-height`: The popup's height, as its content lays it out: a design gives the positioner `height: var(--positioner-height)` to animate a change of size.
- popup: The menu itself: the list of items.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-starting-style`: Present for the first style of its entrance: what it animates in from.
    - `data-ending-style`: Present through its exit: what it animates out to. It leaves the page when the motion ends.
    - `data-side="top | right | bottom | left | inline-start | inline-end"`: The side of the anchor it is on, after any flip. Asked for as `inline-start` or `inline-end`, it says one of those two when it is beside its anchor.
    - `data-align="start | center | end"`: How it is aligned with the anchor.
    - `data-instant="click | dismiss | group"`: Present when it opened or closed in a way that should skip the motion: `click` when the keyboard pressed its trigger or an item, `dismiss` when Escape closed it, `group` when focus or the pointer went from one menu of a bar to another.
- arrow: An element that points at the trigger.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-side="top | right | bottom | left | inline-start | inline-end"`: The side of the anchor it is on, after any flip. Asked for as `inline-start` or `inline-end`, it says one of those two when it is beside its anchor.
    - `data-align="start | center | end"`: How it is aligned with the anchor.
    - `data-uncentered`: Present when the arrow cannot sit at the trigger's centre.
- item: An action. Choosing it closes the menu.
    - `data-highlighted`: Present on the item the pointer or the keyboard is on.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- linkItem: An item that is a link. Choosing it follows the link and closes the menu.
    - `data-highlighted`: Present on the item the pointer or the keyboard is on.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- checkboxItem: An item that is checked or not. Choosing it leaves the menu open.
    - `data-checked`: Present when it is checked.
    - `data-unchecked`: Present when it is not checked.
    - `data-highlighted`: Present on the item the pointer or the keyboard is on.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- checkboxItemIndicator: A mark a checkbox item shows while it is checked.
    - `data-checked`: Present when it is checked.
    - `data-unchecked`: Present when it is not checked.
- radioGroup: Radio items of which one is chosen.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- radioItem: One choice of a radio group. Choosing it leaves the menu open.
    - `data-checked`: Present when it is checked.
    - `data-unchecked`: Present when it is not checked.
    - `data-highlighted`: Present on the item the pointer or the keyboard is on.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- radioItemIndicator: A mark a radio item shows while it is the chosen one.
    - `data-checked`: Present when it is checked.
    - `data-unchecked`: Present when it is not checked.
- submenuTrigger: An item that opens a menu beside it.
    - `data-popup-open`: Present when its menu is open.
    - `data-highlighted`: Present on the item the pointer or the keyboard is on.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.

These parts write no state attribute or CSS variable of their own: `group`, `groupLabel` and `separator`.

### Menubar

```
import "@kirana-ui/web/menubar"
```

`<kui-menubar>`: `<kui-menubar>` around `kui-part="root"` and its `<kui-menu>`s, which work as one: the arrows move between them, and with one open the pointer opens the next. `loop-focus`, `disabled`, `orientation`, `modal`.

Attributes of the element (each also a property, in camel case):

- `loop-focus` (boolean): Whether the arrows go round from the last menu to the first. Default: they do.
- `disabled` (boolean): No menu of the bar opens.
- `orientation` (string): A row (the default) or a column of menus. In a column a menu opens beside its trigger.
- `modal` (boolean): Holds the page while one of its menus is open, as a menu's own `modal` does: its scroll is locked, and a press outside closes the menu and reaches nothing. Default: it does not. Read as a menu opens.

Parts (`kui-part`), each with the `kui-` attributes its element is read for:

- `root`

Anatomy:

```
<kui-menubar>
  root
```

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- root: The row of menus. A menu inside it is one of its items.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-modal`: Present when its menus hold the page while one is open.
    - `data-has-submenu-open`: Present while one of its menus is open.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: Whether its menus are in a row or a column.

### MessageScroller

```
import "@kirana-ui/web/message-scroller"
```

`<kui-message-scroller>`: `<kui-message-scroller>` around `kui-part="root"`, a `viewport` with its `content`, and a `button` that goes back to the newest. It stays at the bottom as content comes, unless the reader has scrolled away. `initial`, `threshold`; it tells `at-bottom-change`.

Attributes of the element (each also a property, in camel case):

- `initial` (string): Where it begins: at the newest message (the default), or at the first.
- `threshold` (number): How near the end counts as at it, in pixels. Default: 24.

Events:

- `at-bottom-change`: `event.detail.atBottom`, with `event.detail.details`. It reports something that happened: there is nothing to keep.

Parts (`kui-part`), each with the `kui-` attributes its element is read for:

- `root`
- `viewport`
- `content`
- `button`

Anatomy:

```
<kui-message-scroller>
  root
    viewport
      content
    button
```

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- root: What holds the conversation and its button.
    - `data-at-bottom`: Present while the newest message is in view.
- viewport: What scrolls: a log, reached by the keyboard.
    - `data-at-bottom`: Present while the newest message is in view.
- button: Goes to the newest message. Inert while that is in view.
    - `data-at-bottom`: Present while the newest message is in view.

This part writes no state attribute or CSS variable of its own: `content`.

### Meter

```
import "@kirana-ui/web/meter"
```

`<kui-meter>`: `<kui-meter>` around `kui-part="root"`, a `label`, a `track` with its `indicator`, and a `value`, which says the value as it is written unless the page gave it something to say. `value`, `min`, `max`, `locale`; `format` and `getAriaValueText` as properties.

Attributes of the element (each also a property, in camel case):

- `value` (number): The measure, between `min` and `max`. A meter always has one.
- `min` (number): Default 0.
- `max` (number): Default 100.
- `locale` (string): The language the value is written in; the page's by default.

Properties only:

- `format`: How the value is written; a percentage of the range by default.
- `getAriaValueText`: What assistive technology reads for the value, when the written value is not enough.

Parts (`kui-part`), each with the `kui-` attributes its element is read for:

- `root`
- `label`
- `track`
- `indicator`
- `value`

Anatomy:

```
<kui-meter>
  root
    track
      indicator
    value
    label
```

These parts write no state attribute or CSS variable of their own: `root`, `track`, `indicator`, `value` and `label`.

### NavigationMenu

```
import "@kirana-ui/web/navigation-menu"
```

`<kui-navigation-menu>`: `<kui-navigation-menu>` around a `kui-part="root"` nav with its `list`. An `item` has a `trigger` (with an `icon` if it has one; `kui-disabled`) and a `content`, which is drawn in the menu's one `viewport` while its item is open; its `kui-value` tells it from the others, and an item that is given none makes its own. A `link` is a link (`kui-active`, `kui-close-on-select="false"`). The viewport is in a `portal` with a `positioner` around the `popup`, with an `arrow` and a `backdrop` if it has them. `value`, `default-value`, `delay`, `close-delay`, `orientation`; it tells `value-change`.

Attributes of the element (each also a property, in camel case):

- `value` (string): The item whose content is shown; `null` is "none".
- `default-value` (string): The item whose content it starts with, when the caller does not hold `value`. Read once.
- `delay` (number): How long the pointer rests on a trigger before its content shows, in milliseconds.
- `close-delay` (number): How long after the pointer leaves the content goes, in milliseconds.
- `orientation` (string): Whether the triggers are laid out across (the default) or down: the arrows that move between them follow.

Events:

- `value-change`: `event.detail.value`, with `event.detail.details`. `preventDefault()` keeps `value` as it was.

Parts (`kui-part`), each with the `kui-` attributes its element is read for:

- `root`
- `list`
- `item`: `kui-value`
- `trigger`: `kui-value`
- `icon`: `kui-value`
- `content`: `kui-value`
- `link`: `kui-active`, `kui-close-on-select`
- `positioner`: `kui-align`, `kui-align-offset`, `kui-anchor`, `kui-arrow-padding`, `kui-collision-boundary`, `kui-collision-padding`, `kui-position-method`, `kui-side`, `kui-side-offset`, `kui-sticky`
- `popup`
- `viewport`
- `arrow`
- `backdrop`

Anatomy:

```
<kui-navigation-menu>
  root
    list
      item (repeated)
        trigger
          icon
        content
          link (repeated)
        link (repeated, as above)
      link (repeated, as above)
    portal
      positioner
        popup
          viewport
          arrow
      backdrop
```

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- root: The navigation.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: Whether the list is a row or a column.
    - `data-open`: Present while an item's content is shown.
    - `data-nested`: Present on a navigation menu inside another's content: a submenu of it.
- list: The row of items.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: Whether the list is a row or a column.
    - `data-open`: Present while an item's content is shown.
- trigger: The button that shows an item's content.
    - `data-popup-open`: Present while the item's content is shown.
    - `data-pressed`: Present while its popup is open: it stays pressed, as a button held down.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- icon: A mark on a trigger that shows whether its content is open.
    - `data-popup-open`: Present while the item's content is shown.
- content: What an item shows. It is drawn in the viewport every item shares.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-starting-style`: Present for the first style of its entrance: what it animates in from.
    - `data-ending-style`: Present through its exit: what it animates out to. It leaves the page when the motion ends.
    - `data-activation-direction="left | right | up | down"`: Which way it came from: the item before it, or after; `up` and `down` when the list is a column.
- link: A link, in the list or in an item's content.
    - `data-active`: Present on the link of the page the reader is on.
- positioner: Places the popup against the open item's trigger. It carries the geometry.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-side="top | right | bottom | left | inline-start | inline-end"`: The side of the anchor it is on, after any flip. Asked for as `inline-start` or `inline-end`, it says one of those two when it is beside its anchor.
    - `data-align="start | center | end"`: How it is aligned with the anchor.
    - `data-anchor-hidden`: Present while the anchor is out of view: scrolled away, or clipped by a box around it.
    - `data-instant`: Present while it should move at once: as it is first drawn, and while the window is resized.
    - `--anchor-width`: The anchor's width.
    - `--anchor-height`: The anchor's height.
    - `--available-width`: The width between the anchor and the edge of the viewport.
    - `--available-height`: The height between the anchor and the edge of the viewport.
    - `--transform-origin`: The point of the popup nearest its anchor, to scale from.
    - `--positioner-width`: The open content's width.
    - `--positioner-height`: The open content's height.
- popup: The panel every item's content is shown in.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-starting-style`: Present for the first style of its entrance: what it animates in from.
    - `data-ending-style`: Present through its exit: what it animates out to. It leaves the page when the motion ends.
    - `data-side="top | right | bottom | left | inline-start | inline-end"`: The side of the anchor it is on, after any flip. Asked for as `inline-start` or `inline-end`, it says one of those two when it is beside its anchor.
    - `data-align="start | center | end"`: How it is aligned with the anchor.
    - `data-anchor-hidden`: Present while the anchor is out of view: scrolled away, or clipped by a box around it.
    - `--popup-width`: The open content's width.
    - `--popup-height`: The open content's height.
- arrow: An element that points at the open item's trigger.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-side="top | right | bottom | left | inline-start | inline-end"`: The side of the anchor it is on, after any flip. Asked for as `inline-start` or `inline-end`, it says one of those two when it is beside its anchor.
    - `data-align="start | center | end"`: How it is aligned with the anchor.
    - `data-uncentered`: Present when the arrow cannot sit at the trigger's centre.
- backdrop: An element behind the popup, for a design that dims the page.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-starting-style`: Present for the first style of its entrance: what it animates in from.
    - `data-ending-style`: Present through its exit: what it animates out to. It leaves the page when the motion ends.

These parts write no state attribute or CSS variable of their own: `item` and `viewport`.

### NumberField

```
import "@kirana-ui/web/number-field"
```

`<kui-number-field>`: `<kui-number-field>` around `kui-part="root"`, a `group`, an `input`, and `increment` and `decrement` buttons. With a name, the root draws the hidden input a form reads. A `scrub-area` (a label, as a rule) is pressed and dragged to change the number, with `kui-direction="vertical"`, `kui-pixel-sensitivity` and `kui-teleport-distance` on it; a `scrub-area-cursor` inside it is drawn at the end of the page while the pointer is locked. `value`, `default-value`, `min`, `max`, `step`, `small-step`, `large-step`, `snap-on-step`, `allow-wheel-scrub`, `locale`, `disabled`, `read-only`, `required`, `name`, `form`; `format` as a property; it tells `value-change` and `value-committed`.

Attributes of the element (each also a property, in camel case):

- `value` (number): The number; `null` is "none".
- `default-value` (number): The value it starts with, when the caller does not hold `value`. Read once.
- `min` (number): The least the number may be.
- `max` (number): The most the number may be.
- `step` (number): What the buttons and the arrows move by. Default 1.
- `small-step` (number): With Alt held. Default 0.1.
- `large-step` (number): With Shift held. Default 10.
- `snap-on-step` (boolean): A step lands on a multiple of the step, counted from `min`.
- `allow-wheel-scrub` (boolean): The wheel steps it while the pointer is over the input and focus is in it.
- `locale` (string): The language it is written in; the page's by default.
- `disabled` (boolean): Disabled: it cannot be changed.
- `read-only` (boolean): Shown as it is, focusable, not changeable.
- `required` (boolean): Needed: in a `Field`, leaving it empty is then invalid.
- `name` (string): With a name, the number is submitted with the form around it.
- `form` (string): The id of the form the control belongs to, when it is not inside it.
- `kui-id` (string): What its input's id is made from: the input is `<id>-input`, which a `<label for>` names. Inside a `Field`, the input takes the field's id instead.

Properties only:

- `format`: How the number is written.

Events:

- `value-change`: `event.detail.value`, with `event.detail.details`. `preventDefault()` keeps `value` as it was.
- `value-committed`: `event.detail.value`, with `event.detail.details`. It reports something that happened: there is nothing to keep.

Parts (`kui-part`), each with the `kui-` attributes its element is read for:

- `root`
- `group`
- `input`
- `increment`
- `decrement`
- `scrub-area`: `kui-direction`, `kui-pixel-sensitivity`, `kui-teleport-distance`
- `scrub-area-cursor`

Anatomy:

```
<kui-number-field>
  root
    group
      input
      increment
      decrement
    scrub-area
      scrub-area-cursor
```

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- root: Groups the number field's parts.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when the number cannot be changed.
    - `data-required`: Present when a number must be given.
    - `data-touched`: Present once focus has left the input.
    - `data-dirty`: Present while the number is not the one it started with.
    - `data-filled`: Present while there is a number.
    - `data-focused`: Present while the input has focus.
    - `data-scrubbing`: Present while the number is dragged from its scrub area.
    - `data-valid`: In a field: present once the number was checked and found right.
    - `data-invalid`: In a field: present while the number is wrong.
- group: What holds the input and its buttons, as one control.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when the number cannot be changed.
    - `data-required`: Present when a number must be given.
    - `data-touched`: Present once focus has left the input.
    - `data-dirty`: Present while the number is not the one it started with.
    - `data-filled`: Present while there is a number.
    - `data-focused`: Present while the input has focus.
    - `data-scrubbing`: Present while the number is dragged from its scrub area.
    - `data-valid`: In a field: present once the number was checked and found right.
    - `data-invalid`: In a field: present while the number is wrong.
- input: The text input: it takes what its locale writes a number with.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when the number cannot be changed.
    - `data-required`: Present when a number must be given.
    - `data-touched`: Present once focus has left the input.
    - `data-dirty`: Present while the number is not the one it started with.
    - `data-filled`: Present while there is a number.
    - `data-focused`: Present while the input has focus.
    - `data-scrubbing`: Present while the number is dragged from its scrub area.
    - `data-valid`: In a field: present once the number was checked and found right.
    - `data-invalid`: In a field: present while the number is wrong.
- increment: A button that steps the number up. Held, it goes on.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when the number cannot be changed.
    - `data-required`: Present when a number must be given.
    - `data-touched`: Present once focus has left the input.
    - `data-dirty`: Present while the number is not the one it started with.
    - `data-filled`: Present while there is a number.
    - `data-focused`: Present while the input has focus.
    - `data-scrubbing`: Present while the number is dragged from its scrub area.
    - `data-valid`: In a field: present once the number was checked and found right.
    - `data-invalid`: In a field: present while the number is wrong.
- decrement: A button that steps the number down. Held, it goes on.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when the number cannot be changed.
    - `data-required`: Present when a number must be given.
    - `data-touched`: Present once focus has left the input.
    - `data-dirty`: Present while the number is not the one it started with.
    - `data-filled`: Present while there is a number.
    - `data-focused`: Present while the input has focus.
    - `data-scrubbing`: Present while the number is dragged from its scrub area.
    - `data-valid`: In a field: present once the number was checked and found right.
    - `data-invalid`: In a field: present while the number is wrong.
- scrubArea: An area that is pressed and dragged to change the number: the field's label, as a rule. It takes `direction`, `pixelSensitivity` and `teleportDistance`. A mouse's pointer is locked for the drag where the browser has that (not in Safari); a finger drags as it is.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when the number cannot be changed.
    - `data-required`: Present when a number must be given.
    - `data-touched`: Present once focus has left the input.
    - `data-dirty`: Present while the number is not the one it started with.
    - `data-filled`: Present while there is a number.
    - `data-focused`: Present while the input has focus.
    - `data-scrubbing`: Present while the number is dragged from its scrub area.
    - `data-valid`: In a field: present once the number was checked and found right.
    - `data-invalid`: In a field: present while the number is wrong.
- scrubAreaCursor: What is drawn in place of the pointer while it is locked for a drag: in the page only then, at the end of `<body>`, placed by the component.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when the number cannot be changed.
    - `data-required`: Present when a number must be given.
    - `data-touched`: Present once focus has left the input.
    - `data-dirty`: Present while the number is not the one it started with.
    - `data-filled`: Present while there is a number.
    - `data-focused`: Present while the input has focus.
    - `data-scrubbing`: Present while the number is dragged from its scrub area.
    - `data-valid`: In a field: present once the number was checked and found right.
    - `data-invalid`: In a field: present while the number is wrong.

### Otp

```
import "@kirana-ui/web/otp"
```

`<kui-otp>`: `<kui-otp>` around `kui-part="root"`, the one `input` that is typed in, and a `slot` for each character (`kui-index`, from 0), which says its character and may hold a `caret`, in the page while the next character goes there. Slots may be in `group`s with a `separator` between. `length`, `value`, `default-value`, `validation-type`, `pattern`, `disabled`, `read-only`, `required`, `name`, `form`; it tells `value-change` and `value-complete`.

Attributes of the element (each also a property, in camel case):

- `length` (number): How many characters the code has. Default: 6.
- `value` (string): The characters typed so far, when the caller holds them.
- `default-value` (string): The characters it starts with, when the caller does not hold `value`. Read once.
- `validation-type` (string): What a character may be: a digit (`numeric`), a letter (`alpha`, `a` to `z` either case), either (`alphanumeric`), or anything but white space (`none`: no rule beyond that). It also says which keyboard a phone shows: the digits' for `numeric`, letters' otherwise. Default: `numeric`, on purpose: a one-time code is digits, and its keyboard is then the one to type them on. `alphabetic` and `text` are older spellings of `alpha` and `none`, still read.
- `pattern` (string): What else a character may be: a regular expression, as text, that one character must match whole (`"[A-F0-9]"`), in place of `validationType`'s rule. Text, as an attribute can only be, so it is given the same way on every framework and on a custom element. With a pattern, `validationType` only says the keyboard, and defaults to `none`.
- `disabled` (boolean): Disabled: it cannot be changed.
- `read-only` (boolean): Shown as it is, focusable, not changeable.
- `required` (boolean): Needed: in a `Field`, an empty code is then invalid.
- `name` (string): With a name, the code is submitted with the form around it.
- `form` (string): The id of the form the input belongs to, when it is not inside it.
- `kui-id` (string): The id of its input, not of the root: a `<label for>` names it.

Events:

- `value-change`: `event.detail.value`, with `event.detail.details`. `preventDefault()` keeps `value` as it was.
- `value-complete`: `event.detail.value`, with `event.detail.details`. It reports something that happened: there is nothing to keep.

Parts (`kui-part`), each with the `kui-` attributes its element is read for:

- `root`
- `input`
- `group`
- `separator`
- `slot`: `kui-index`
- `caret`: `kui-index`

Anatomy:

```
<kui-otp>
  root
    input
    group (repeated)
      slot (repeated)
        caret
    separator (repeated)
```

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- root: The code: the input and its cells.
    - `data-touched`: Inside a Field: present once focus has left the control.
    - `data-dirty`: Inside a Field: present while the value is not the one it started with.
    - `data-filled`: Present when the code has a character in it.
    - `data-focused`: Present while the input has focus.
    - `data-valid`: Inside a Field: present once the value has been checked and found right.
    - `data-invalid`: Inside a Field: present while the value is wrong.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when it can be read but not changed.
    - `data-required`: Present when the form needs it.
    - `data-complete`: Present when every character is in.
- input: The one input the code is typed in. A design lays it over the cells, unseen.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- slot: One cell of the code.
    - `data-index`: The cell's place, from 0.
    - `data-active`: Present on the cell the next character goes in, or that is selected.
    - `data-touched`: Inside a Field: present once focus has left the control.
    - `data-dirty`: Inside a Field: present while the value is not the one it started with.
    - `data-filled`: Present when the cell has its character.
    - `data-focused`: Present while the input has focus.
    - `data-valid`: Inside a Field: present once the value has been checked and found right.
    - `data-invalid`: Inside a Field: present while the value is wrong.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when it can be read but not changed.
    - `data-required`: Present when the form needs it.
    - `data-complete`: Present when every character is in.

These parts write no state attribute or CSS variable of their own: `group`, `separator` and `caret`.

### Pagination

```
import "@kirana-ui/web/pagination"
```

`<kui-pagination>`: `<kui-pagination>` around a `kui-part="root"` nav with `previous` and `next` buttons and, between them, a `<template kui-each="items">` holding an `item` button for a page (`kui-when="page"`; `{page}` is its number) and an `ellipsis` for a gap (`kui-when="ellipsis"`; `{key}` is `start` or `end`). `page`, `default-page`, `count`, `page-size`, `sibling-count`, `boundary-count`, `disabled`; it tells `page-change`.

Attributes of the element (each also a property, in camel case):

- `page` (number): The page shown, from 1.
- `default-page` (number): The page it starts at, when the caller does not hold `page`. Read once.
- `count` (number): How many items there are in all.
- `page-size` (number): How many items a page holds. Default 10.
- `sibling-count` (number): How many pages are listed each side of the one shown. Default 1.
- `boundary-count` (number): How many pages are always listed at each end. Default 1.
- `disabled` (boolean): Disabled: no page can be gone to.

Events:

- `page-change`: `event.detail.page`, with `event.detail.details`. `preventDefault()` keeps `page` as it was.

Parts (`kui-part`), each with the `kui-` attributes its element is read for:

- `root`
- `previous`
- `next`
- `ellipsis`
- `item`

Lists (`<template kui-each="…">`): `items`.

Anatomy:

```
<kui-pagination>
  root
    <template kui-each="items">
      item (repeated)
      ellipsis (repeated)
    previous
    next
```

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- root: The pages of a list, as a navigation.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- item: A page: pressed, it is the one shown.
    - `data-selected`: Present on the page that is shown.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- previous: Goes to the page before.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- next: Goes to the page after.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.

This part writes no state attribute or CSS variable of its own: `ellipsis`.

### PasswordInput

```
import "@kirana-ui/web/password-input"
```

`<kui-password-input>`: `<kui-password-input>` around `kui-part="root"`, an `input`, and a `toggle` button that shows the password and hides it again, with an `indicator` inside that says which it is. Inside a `<kui-field>` the input is the field's control. `visible`, `default-visible`, `disabled`; `toggleLabels` (`{ show, hide }`, the toggle's names) as a property, which an `aria-label` on the toggle wins over. It tells `visible-change` and `value-change`.

Attributes of the element (each also a property, in camel case):

- `visible` (boolean): Whether the password can be read, when the caller holds it.
- `default-visible` (boolean): Read once. Default `false`.
- `disabled` (boolean): Disabled: nothing can be typed in it.

Properties only:

- `toggleLabels`: What the toggle is called, for assistive technology: `show` while the password is hidden, `hide` while it is shown. Default: `"Show password"` and `"Hide password"`. An `aria-label` given to the toggle itself wins over both.

Events:

- `visible-change`: `event.detail.visible`, with `event.detail.details`. `preventDefault()` keeps `visible` as it was.
- `value-change`: `event.detail.value`, with `event.detail.details`. It reports something that happened: there is nothing to keep.

Parts (`kui-part`), each with the `kui-` attributes its element is read for:

- `root`
- `input`
- `toggle`
- `indicator`

Anatomy:

```
<kui-password-input>
  root
    input
    toggle
      indicator (optional)
```

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- root: A password that can be shown while it is typed.
    - `data-visible`: Present while the password can be read.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- input: The `<input>`: a password, or text while it is shown. In a `Field` it is the field's control.
    - `data-visible`: Present while the password can be read.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-touched`: Present once focus has left it.
    - `data-dirty`: Present once its text differs from what it began with.
    - `data-filled`: Present while it holds text.
    - `data-focused`: Present while it has focus.
    - `data-valid`: In a field: present once the value was checked and found right.
    - `data-invalid`: In a field: present while the value is wrong.
- toggle: Shows the password, and hides it again. Focus and the caret stay in the input. It is named "Show password" while the password is hidden and "Hide password" while it is shown: the root's `toggleLabels` (`{ show, hide }`) words them in the page's language, and an `aria-label` given to the toggle wins over both.
    - `data-visible`: Present while the password can be read.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- indicator: An element hidden from assistive technology (`aria-hidden`) that holds what the design draws to say which of the two it is, an eye open or struck, by its `data-visible`. It has no content of its own.
    - `data-visible`: Present while the password can be read.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.

### Popover

```
import "@kirana-ui/web/popover"
```

`<kui-popover>`: `<kui-popover>` around a `kui-part="trigger"` button and a `portal`, drawn at the end of the page while it is open, with a `positioner` (`kui-side`, `kui-align`, `kui-side-offset`, `kui-align-offset`, `kui-collision-padding`, and `kui-anchor`: the id of the element it is placed against, when that is not the trigger) around the `popup`, which may hold an `arrow`, a `title`, a `description` and a `close` button; the portal may hold a `backdrop` too. The trigger takes `kui-open-on-hover`, with `kui-delay` and `kui-close-delay`. `open`, `default-open`, `modal` (there, or `"trap-focus"`); it tells `open-change`.

Attributes of the element (each also a property, in camel case):

- `open` (boolean): Whether it is open, when the caller holds it.
- `default-open` (boolean): Whether it starts open, when the caller does not hold `open`. Read once.
- `modal` (string): What the page behind it may do while it is open. `false` (the default): everything. `true`: nothing, the page is inert and does not scroll, and Tab stays inside the popover. `"trap-focus"`: Tab stays inside the popover, and the page can still be pressed and scrolled. A popover the pointer opened holds nothing until it is pressed. Read as it opens.

Events:

- `open-change`: `event.detail.open`, with `event.detail.details`. `preventDefault()` keeps `open` as it was.

Parts (`kui-part`), each with the `kui-` attributes its element is read for:

- `trigger`: `kui-close-delay`, `kui-delay`, `kui-open-on-hover`
- `backdrop`
- `positioner`: `kui-align`, `kui-align-offset`, `kui-anchor`, `kui-arrow-padding`, `kui-collision-boundary`, `kui-collision-padding`, `kui-position-method`, `kui-side`, `kui-side-offset`, `kui-sticky`
- `popup`
- `arrow`
- `title`
- `description`
- `close`

Anatomy:

```
<kui-popover>
  trigger
  portal
    backdrop
    positioner
      popup
        title
        description
        close
        arrow
```

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- trigger: The button that opens the popover, and what it is placed against.
    - `data-popup-open`: Present when the popover is open.
    - `data-pressed`: Present while the popover a press on this trigger opened is open: it stays pressed, as a button held down.
- backdrop: A layer over the page behind the popover.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-starting-style`: Present for the first style of its entrance: what it animates in from.
    - `data-ending-style`: Present through its exit: what it animates out to. It leaves the page when the motion ends.
- positioner: Places the popup against the trigger. It carries the geometry.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-side="top | right | bottom | left | inline-start | inline-end"`: The side of the anchor it is on, after any flip. Asked for as `inline-start` or `inline-end`, it says one of those two when it is beside its anchor.
    - `data-align="start | center | end"`: How it is aligned with the anchor.
    - `data-anchor-hidden`: Present while the anchor is out of view: scrolled away, or clipped by a box around it.
    - `--anchor-width`: The anchor's width.
    - `--anchor-height`: The anchor's height.
    - `--available-width`: The width between the anchor and the edge of the viewport.
    - `--available-height`: The height between the anchor and the edge of the viewport.
    - `--transform-origin`: The point of the popup nearest its anchor, to scale from.
    - `--positioner-width`: The popup's width, as its content lays it out: a design gives the positioner `width: var(--positioner-width)` to animate a change of size.
    - `--positioner-height`: The popup's height, as its content lays it out: a design gives the positioner `height: var(--positioner-height)` to animate a change of size.
- popup: The popover itself.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-starting-style`: Present for the first style of its entrance: what it animates in from.
    - `data-ending-style`: Present through its exit: what it animates out to. It leaves the page when the motion ends.
    - `data-side="top | right | bottom | left | inline-start | inline-end"`: The side of the anchor it is on, after any flip. Asked for as `inline-start` or `inline-end`, it says one of those two when it is beside its anchor.
    - `data-align="start | center | end"`: How it is aligned with the anchor.
    - `data-instant="click | dismiss"`: Present when it opened or closed in a way that should skip the motion: `click` when the keyboard pressed the trigger, `dismiss` when Escape closed it.
    - `--popup-width`: Its width: `auto`, and while its content changes size, the old width and then the new one, for a transition between them.
    - `--popup-height`: Its height: `auto`, and while its content changes size, the old height and then the new one, for a transition between them.
- arrow: An element that points at the trigger, placed along the popup's edge.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-side="top | right | bottom | left | inline-start | inline-end"`: The side of the anchor it is on, after any flip. Asked for as `inline-start` or `inline-end`, it says one of those two when it is beside its anchor.
    - `data-align="start | center | end"`: How it is aligned with the anchor.
    - `data-uncentered`: Present when the popup was pushed along its edge, so the arrow is not at the trigger's centre.

These parts write no state attribute or CSS variable of their own: `title`, `description` and `close`.

### Progress

```
import "@kirana-ui/web/progress"
```

`<kui-progress>`: `<kui-progress>` around `kui-part="root"`, a `label`, a `track` with its `indicator`, and a `value`, which says the value as it is written unless the page gave it something to say. `value` (left out: not known yet), `min`, `max`, `locale`; `format` and `getAriaValueText` as properties.

Attributes of the element (each also a property, in camel case):

- `value` (number): The value. For a progress bar, `null` is "under way, how far is not known".
- `min` (number): Default 0.
- `max` (number): Default 100.
- `locale` (string): The language the value is written in; the page's by default.

Properties only:

- `format`: How the value is written; a percentage of the range by default.
- `getAriaValueText`: What assistive technology reads for the value, when the written value is not enough.

Parts (`kui-part`), each with the `kui-` attributes its element is read for:

- `root`
- `label`
- `track`
- `indicator`
- `value`

Anatomy:

```
<kui-progress>
  root
    track
      indicator
    value
    label
```

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- root: The progress bar: it says the value to assistive technology.
    - `data-progressing`: Present while the task is under way.
    - `data-complete`: Present once the value has reached the end of the range.
    - `data-indeterminate`: Present while how far the task has come is not known.
- track: The whole range.
    - `data-progressing`: Present while the task is under way.
    - `data-complete`: Present once the value has reached the end of the range.
    - `data-indeterminate`: Present while how far the task has come is not known.
- indicator: The filled part: its width is the value's share of the range.
    - `data-progressing`: Present while the task is under way.
    - `data-complete`: Present once the value has reached the end of the range.
    - `data-indeterminate`: Present while how far the task has come is not known.
- value: The value, written.
    - `data-progressing`: Present while the task is under way.
    - `data-complete`: Present once the value has reached the end of the range.
    - `data-indeterminate`: Present while how far the task has come is not known.
- label: The bar's name.
    - `data-progressing`: Present while the task is under way.
    - `data-complete`: Present once the value has reached the end of the range.
    - `data-indeterminate`: Present while how far the task has come is not known.

### QrCode

import "@kirana-ui/web/qr-code"

`<kui-qr-code>`: `<kui-qr-code>` around `kui-part="root"`, a `frame` (an `<svg>`) and its `pattern` (a `<path>`). `value`, `correction`.

Attributes of the element (each also a property, in camel case):

- `value` (string): What the code says: a link, a text. Written as UTF-8.
- `correction` (string): How much of it may be lost and still be read. Default: `"M"`.

Parts (`kui-part`), each with the `kui-` attributes its element is read for:

- `root`
- `frame`
- `pattern`

Anatomy:

```
<kui-qr-code>
  root
    frame
      pattern
```

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- root: What holds the code.
    - `data-invalid`: Present when the value is longer than a code holds.

These parts write no state attribute or CSS variable of their own: `frame` and `pattern`.

### RadioGroup

```
import "@kirana-ui/web/radio-group"
```

`<kui-radio-group>`: `<kui-radio-group>` around `kui-part="root"` and an `item` button for each `value`, with an `indicator` inside that is in the page while its item is the chosen one. An item draws the hidden native radio a form and a label reach; an item's `kui-id` is that radio's id, which a `<label for>` names. `value`, `default-value`, `disabled`, `read-only`, `required`, `name`, `form`; it tells `value-change`.

Attributes of the element (each also a property, in camel case):

- `value` (string): The chosen value; `null` is "none".
- `default-value` (string): The value it starts with, when the caller does not hold `value`. Read once.
- `disabled` (boolean): Disables every item of the group.
- `read-only` (boolean): Shown as it is, focusable, not changeable.
- `required` (boolean): Needed: in a `Field`, choosing none is then invalid.
- `name` (string): With a name, the chosen value is submitted with the form around the group.
- `form` (string): The id of the form the control belongs to, when it is not inside it.

Events:

- `value-change`: `event.detail.value`, with `event.detail.details`. `preventDefault()` keeps `value` as it was.

Parts (`kui-part`), each with the `kui-` attributes its element is read for:

- `root`
- `item`: `kui-disabled`, `kui-id`, `kui-value`
- `indicator`: `kui-value`

Anatomy:

```
<kui-radio-group>
  root
    item (repeated)
      indicator
```

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- root: Groups the items: one of them is chosen at most.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when it can be read but not changed.
    - `data-required`: Present when the form needs it.
    - `data-touched`: Inside a Field: present once focus has left the control.
    - `data-dirty`: Inside a Field: present while the value is not the one it started with.
    - `data-filled`: Inside a Field: present while the control has a value.
    - `data-focused`: Inside a Field: present while the control has focus.
    - `data-valid`: Inside a Field: present once the value has been checked and found right.
    - `data-invalid`: Inside a Field: present while the value is wrong.
- item: One choice. It holds a hidden native radio, which a form and a label reach: the item's `id` (`kpId` on Angular, `kui-id` on a custom element) is the radio's, which a `<label for>` names.
    - `data-checked`: Present when it is checked.
    - `data-unchecked`: Present when it is not checked.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when it can be read but not changed.
    - `data-required`: Present when the form needs it.
    - `data-touched`: Inside a Field: present once focus has left the control.
    - `data-dirty`: Inside a Field: present while the value is not the one it started with.
    - `data-filled`: Inside a Field: present while the control has a value.
    - `data-focused`: Inside a Field: present while the control has focus.
    - `data-valid`: Inside a Field: present once the value has been checked and found right.
    - `data-invalid`: Inside a Field: present while the value is wrong.
- indicator: The mark. In the page while its item is the chosen one.
    - `data-checked`: Present when it is checked.
    - `data-unchecked`: Present when it is not checked.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when it can be read but not changed.
    - `data-required`: Present when the form needs it.
    - `data-touched`: Inside a Field: present once focus has left the control.
    - `data-dirty`: Inside a Field: present while the value is not the one it started with.
    - `data-filled`: Inside a Field: present while the control has a value.
    - `data-focused`: Inside a Field: present while the control has focus.
    - `data-valid`: Inside a Field: present once the value has been checked and found right.
    - `data-invalid`: Inside a Field: present while the value is wrong.
    - `data-starting-style`: Present for the first style of its entrance: what it animates in from.
    - `data-ending-style`: Present through its exit: what it animates out to. It leaves the page when the motion ends.

### Rating

```
import "@kirana-ui/web/rating"
```

`<kui-rating>`: `<kui-rating>` around a `kui-part="root"` element holding a `<template kui-each="items">` with an `item` for a place (`{place}` is its number, from 1). The root draws the hidden input a form reads, as its last child. `value`, `default-value`, `count`, `allow-half`, `disabled`, `read-only`, `required`, `name`, `form`; it tells `value-change` and `hover-change`.

Attributes of the element (each also a property, in camel case):

- `value` (number): How much is given, from 0 (none) to `count`; a half where `allowHalf` is set.
- `default-value` (number): The value it starts with, when the caller does not hold `value`. Read once.
- `count` (number): How many items there are. Default 5.
- `allow-half` (boolean): Whether half an item can be given: by the half of it a pointer is over, and by the arrows.
- `disabled` (boolean): Disabled: it cannot be changed.
- `read-only` (boolean): Shown as it is, focusable, not changeable.
- `required` (boolean): Needed: in a `Field`, giving none is then invalid.
- `name` (string): With a name, the value is submitted with the form around it; none is submitted as empty.
- `form` (string): The id of the form the control belongs to, when it is not inside it.

Events:

- `value-change`: `event.detail.value`, with `event.detail.details`. `preventDefault()` keeps `value` as it was.
- `hover-change`: `event.detail.value`, with `event.detail.details`. It reports something that happened: there is nothing to keep.

Parts (`kui-part`), each with the `kui-` attributes its element is read for:

- `root`
- `item`

Lists (`<template kui-each="…">`): `items`.

Anatomy:

```
<kui-rating>
  root
    <template kui-each="items">
      item (repeated)
```

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- root: The items, as one choice: a radio group. It holds the hidden input a form reads.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when it is shown and cannot be changed.
    - `data-required`: Present when a value is needed.
    - `data-hovering`: Present while a pointer is over an item.
- item: One item (a star): pressed, the value is its place, or half of it.
    - `data-checked`: Present on the item that holds the value.
    - `data-filled`: Present on every item up to the value drawn: the one a pointer is over, or the one held.
    - `data-half`: Present on the item the value drawn fills by half, which has `data-filled` too. No variable says how much is filled: a design draws the half, an element of its own in the item (a filled star over an empty one) clipped to its first half: `[data-half] .star-fill { clip-path: inset(0 50% 0 0) }`, `inset(0 0 0 50%)` where the text runs right to left.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when it is shown and cannot be changed.
    - `data-required`: Present when a value is needed.

### Resizable

```
import "@kirana-ui/web/resizable"
```

`<kui-resizable>`: `<kui-resizable>` around `kui-part="group"`, its `panel`s (`kui-default-size`, `kui-min-size`, `kui-max-size`, in shares of a hundred) and a `handle` between two (`kui-disabled`). `orientation`, `keyboard-step`, `disabled`; it tells `sizes-change`.

Attributes of the element (each also a property, in camel case):

- `orientation` (string): Whether the panels are side by side (the default) or one over the other.
- `keyboard-step` (number): How far an arrow key moves a handle, in hundredths of the group. Default: 10.
- `disabled` (boolean): Disabled: the handles cannot be dragged or moved with the keyboard.

Events:

- `sizes-change`: `event.detail.sizes`, with `event.detail.details`. It reports something that happened: there is nothing to keep.

Parts (`kui-part`), each with the `kui-` attributes its element is read for:

- `group`
- `panel`
- `handle`: `kui-disabled`

Anatomy:

```
<kui-resizable>
  group
    panel (repeated)
    handle (repeated)
```

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- group: The panels and the bars between them. A design lays it out as a flex box: `display: flex`, and `flex-direction: column` when it is vertical. A group in a panel that is a flex box itself takes `min-width: 0` and `min-height: 0`, or what it holds widens the panel.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: Whether the panels are side by side or one over the other.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- panel: One panel. It carries its share of the group, written as its `flex` with `min-width: 0` and `min-height: 0`, so what it holds cannot keep it past its share. Its `overflow` is the design's.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: Whether the panels are side by side or one over the other.
    - `--panel-size`: The panel's share, in hundredths of the group.
- handle: The bar between two panels: dragged, or moved with the arrows. A design gives it its thickness and `flex-shrink: 0`, so the panels do not squeeze it.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: Whether the panels are side by side or one over the other.
    - `data-dragging`: Present while the bar is dragged.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.

### ScrollArea

```
import "@kirana-ui/web/scroll-area"
```

`<kui-scroll-area>`: `<kui-scroll-area>` around `kui-part="root"`, a `viewport` with its `content`, a `scrollbar` for each way (`kui-orientation="horizontal"` for the one across) with its `thumb`, and a `corner`. A scrollbar is in the page while there is something to scroll its way. The library places the scrollbars and the corner against the root; the page gives a scrollbar its thickness and draws it.

Parts (`kui-part`), each with the `kui-` attributes its element is read for:

- `root`
- `viewport`
- `content`
- `scrollbar`: `kui-orientation`
- `thumb`: `kui-orientation`
- `corner`

Anatomy:

```
<kui-scroll-area>
  root
    viewport
      content (optional)
      scrollbar (repeated, as above)
    scrollbar (repeated)
      thumb
    corner
```

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- root: The area. It holds the viewport and the scrollbars, which the library places against it: a design gives a scrollbar its thickness and draws it, and places nothing.
    - `data-has-overflow-x`: Present when there is more to see sideways.
    - `data-has-overflow-y`: Present when there is more to see up or down.
    - `data-overflow-x-start`: Present when there is more to scroll to towards the start of a line.
    - `data-overflow-x-end`: Present when there is more to scroll to towards the end of a line.
    - `data-overflow-y-start`: Present when there is more to scroll to above.
    - `data-overflow-y-end`: Present when there is more to scroll to below.
    - `data-scrolling`: Present while it is being scrolled, and a moment after.
    - `data-hovering`: Present while the pointer is over the area.
    - `--scroll-area-corner-width`: The width of the corner: the vertical scrollbar's, while both scrollbars and the corner are in the page.
    - `--scroll-area-corner-height`: The height of the corner: the horizontal scrollbar's, while both scrollbars and the corner are in the page.
- viewport: The element that scrolls.
    - `data-has-overflow-x`: Present when there is more to see sideways.
    - `data-has-overflow-y`: Present when there is more to see up or down.
    - `data-overflow-x-start`: Present when there is more to scroll to towards the start of a line.
    - `data-overflow-x-end`: Present when there is more to scroll to towards the end of a line.
    - `data-overflow-y-start`: Present when there is more to scroll to above.
    - `data-overflow-y-end`: Present when there is more to scroll to below.
    - `data-scrolling`: Present while it is being scrolled, and a moment after.
    - `--scroll-area-overflow-x-start`: How far the view is from the start of a line, to fade that edge by: `0px` at it.
    - `--scroll-area-overflow-x-end`: How far the view is from the end of a line: `0px` at it.
    - `--scroll-area-overflow-y-start`: How far the view is from the top: `0px` at it.
    - `--scroll-area-overflow-y-end`: How far the view is from the bottom: `0px` at it.
- content: A box around what is scrolled, as wide as what it holds. Not needed to measure: the viewport's children are watched as they are. For content whose own box does not grow with what is in it (a block holding a wider table, or bare text).
    - `data-has-overflow-x`: Present when there is more to see sideways.
    - `data-has-overflow-y`: Present when there is more to see up or down.
    - `data-overflow-x-start`: Present when there is more to scroll to towards the start of a line.
    - `data-overflow-x-end`: Present when there is more to scroll to towards the end of a line.
    - `data-overflow-y-start`: Present when there is more to scroll to above.
    - `data-overflow-y-end`: Present when there is more to scroll to below.
    - `data-scrolling`: Present while it is being scrolled, and a moment after.
- scrollbar: A scrollbar's track, placed along its edge of the area. In the page while there is something to scroll its way.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: Which way the scrollbar scrolls.
    - `data-hovering`: Present while the pointer is over the area.
    - `data-scrolling`: Present while the area is scrolled its way.
    - `data-has-overflow-x`: Present when there is more to see sideways.
    - `data-has-overflow-y`: Present when there is more to see up or down.
    - `data-overflow-x-start`: Present when there is more to scroll to towards the start of a line.
    - `data-overflow-x-end`: Present when there is more to scroll to towards the end of a line.
    - `data-overflow-y-start`: Present when there is more to scroll to above.
    - `data-overflow-y-end`: Present when there is more to scroll to below.
    - `--scroll-area-thumb-height`: A vertical thumb's height.
    - `--scroll-area-thumb-width`: A horizontal thumb's width.
- thumb: The part of a scrollbar that shows where the view is, and can be dragged. As long as its scrollbar's variable says.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: Which way the scrollbar scrolls.
    - `data-scrolling`: Present while the area is scrolled its way.

This part writes no state attribute or CSS variable of its own: `corner`.

### Select

```
import "@kirana-ui/web/select"
```

`<kui-select>`: `<kui-select>` around a `kui-part="trigger"` button holding a `value` (it says the chosen item's text, or its `kui-placeholder`; with `multiple`, the chosen items' texts with commas between), and a `portal` with a `positioner` (its `kui-side` and the like, and `kui-align-item-with-trigger`) around the `popup`. The popup holds an `item` for each `kui-value` (`kui-disabled`, `kui-label`), each with an `item-text` and an `item-indicator`; items may be in a `group` with a `group-label`, with `separator`s between, and in a `list` between a `scroll-up-arrow` and a `scroll-down-arrow`. With a name it draws the hidden input a form reads. A `value` part that holds something says what the page wrote there: a `<template kui-each="values">` in it is drawn for each chosen value (`{value}`, `{label}`), in the items' order. `value`, `default-value`, `open`, `default-open`, `disabled`, `read-only`, `required`, `multiple` (with it, `value` and `default-value` hold the chosen values with commas between), `name`, `form`, `presentation` (`sheet` opens the list from the bottom edge, modal, over a `backdrop` part in the portal; `auto` on a narrow touch screen) and `sheet-below`; `items`, `itemToStringLabel` and `itemToStringValue` as properties; it tells `value-change` and `open-change`.

Attributes of the element (each also a property, in camel case):

- `value` (string): The chosen value; `null` is "none". With `multiple`, the chosen values, in the order they were chosen.
- `default-value` (string): The value it starts with (with `multiple`, the values), when the caller does not hold `value`. Read once.
- `open` (boolean): Whether the list is open, when the caller holds it.
- `default-open` (boolean): Whether the list starts open, when the caller does not hold `open`. Read once.
- `disabled` (boolean): Disabled: it cannot be changed.
- `read-only` (boolean): Shown as it is, focusable, not changeable: the list still opens to be read, and no item can be chosen. Its value is still submitted with the form.
- `required` (boolean): In a field, "none" is then wrong.
- `multiple` (boolean): Several values: `value`, `defaultValue` and `onValueChange` then hold a list. Read once.
- `name` (string): With a name, the value is submitted with the form around it.
- `form` (string): The id of the form the control belongs to, when it is not inside it.
- `presentation` (string): How the list opens. `"sheet"`: from the bottom edge, not placed against the trigger, modal with a backdrop, swiped down or pressed outside to close. `"auto"`: decided each time it opens, a sheet when the pointer is coarse and the viewport narrower than `sheetBelow`. Default `"popup"`.
- `sheet-below` (number): With `presentation: "auto"`: the viewport's width, in CSS pixels, under which a coarse pointer opens a sheet. Default 640.

Properties only:

- `items`: The labels of the values, for the trigger to show before the list has ever been opened: a list of values with their labels, or, for values that are text, the labels by value (`{ apple: "Apple" }`). Not needed for the list itself: its items are read from the markup.
- `itemToStringLabel`: For values that are objects: the text the trigger shows for one, and what typing matches an item by when it gives no `label`. Without it, an object's own `label` names it, then the label `items` gives it, then the item's text in the markup.
- `itemToStringValue`: For values that are objects: the text the form is sent for one. Without it, the `value` of an object shaped `{ value, label }` is sent, and any other object as JSON.

Events:

- `value-change`: `event.detail.value`, with `event.detail.details`. `preventDefault()` keeps `value` as it was.
- `open-change`: `event.detail.open`, with `event.detail.details`. `preventDefault()` keeps `open` as it was.

Parts (`kui-part`), each with the `kui-` attributes its element is read for:

- `trigger`
- `value`: `kui-placeholder`
- `positioner`: `kui-align`, `kui-align-item-with-trigger`, `kui-align-offset`, `kui-anchor`, `kui-arrow-padding`, `kui-collision-boundary`, `kui-collision-padding`, `kui-position-method`, `kui-side`, `kui-side-offset`, `kui-sticky`
- `popup`
- `backdrop`
- `list`
- `scroll-up-arrow`
- `scroll-down-arrow`
- `group`: `kui-id`
- `group-label`
- `separator`
- `item`: `kui-disabled`, `kui-label`, `kui-value`
- `item-text`: `kui-value`
- `item-indicator`: `kui-value`

Lists (`<template kui-each="…">`): `values`.

Anatomy:

```
<kui-select>
  trigger
    value
      <template kui-each="values"> (optional)
  portal
    backdrop (optional)
    positioner
      popup
        scroll-up-arrow
        list (optional)
          group (optional, repeated)
            group-label
            item (repeated)
              item-text
              item-indicator
          separator (repeated)
        scroll-down-arrow
```

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- trigger: The button that shows the value and opens the list.
    - `data-popup-open`: Present when the list is open.
    - `data-pressed`: Present while its popup is open: it stays pressed, as a button held down.
    - `data-popup-side="top | right | bottom | left | inline-start | inline-end | none"`: While the list is in the page: the side of the trigger it is on, after any flip; `none` when it lies over the trigger. Not said while it opens as a sheet.
    - `data-placeholder`: Present while nothing is chosen.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when it can be read but not changed.
    - `data-required`: Present when the form needs it.
    - `data-touched`: Inside a Field: present once focus has left the control.
    - `data-dirty`: Inside a Field: present while the value is not the one it started with.
    - `data-filled`: Inside a Field: present while the control has a value.
    - `data-focused`: Inside a Field: present while the control has focus.
    - `data-valid`: Inside a Field: present once the value has been checked and found right.
    - `data-invalid`: Inside a Field: present while the value is wrong.
- value: The chosen value's label, or the placeholder. With several values, their labels with commas between.
    - `data-placeholder`: Present while nothing is chosen.
- backdrop: The layer over the page behind the list: a press on it closes the list.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-starting-style`: Present for the first style of its entrance: what it animates in from.
    - `data-ending-style`: Present through its exit: what it animates out to. It leaves the page when the motion ends.
    - `data-presentation="popup | sheet"`: How the list opened: placed against its trigger, or as a sheet from the bottom edge.
    - `data-swiping`: Present while the sheet is dragged.
    - `data-swipe-dismiss`: Present once a drag has closed it.
    - `--drawer-swipe-movement-x`: As a sheet: how far it has been dragged across, always 0px.
    - `--drawer-swipe-movement-y`: As a sheet: how far it has been dragged down.
    - `--drawer-swipe-progress`: As a sheet: how far it has been dragged, of its own height: 0 to 1.
- positioner: Places the list against the trigger. It carries the geometry. As a sheet it is not placed, and carries none.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-side="top | right | bottom | left | inline-start | inline-end | none"`: The side of the trigger it is on, after any flip; `none` when it lies over the trigger.
    - `data-align="start | center | end"`: How it is aligned with the anchor.
    - `data-presentation="popup | sheet"`: How the list opened: placed against its trigger, or as a sheet from the bottom edge.
    - `data-anchor-hidden`: Present while the anchor is out of view: scrolled away, or clipped by a box around it.
    - `--anchor-width`: The anchor's width.
    - `--anchor-height`: The anchor's height.
    - `--available-width`: The width between the anchor and the edge of the viewport.
    - `--available-height`: The height between the anchor and the edge of the viewport.
    - `--transform-origin`: The point of the popup nearest its anchor, to scale from.
- scrollUpArrow: In the page while there is more of the list above: it scrolls the list while the pointer moves over it.
    - `data-direction="up | down"`: The way it scrolls the list.
    - `data-visible`: Present while there is more of the list its way.
    - `data-side="top | right | bottom | left | inline-start | inline-end | none"`: The side of the trigger the list is on; `none` when it lies over the trigger.
    - `data-starting-style`: Present for the first style of its entrance: what it animates in from.
    - `data-ending-style`: Present through its exit: what it animates out to. It leaves the page when the motion ends.
- scrollDownArrow: In the page while there is more of the list below: it scrolls the list while the pointer moves over it.
    - `data-direction="up | down"`: The way it scrolls the list.
    - `data-visible`: Present while there is more of the list its way.
    - `data-side="top | right | bottom | left | inline-start | inline-end | none"`: The side of the trigger the list is on; `none` when it lies over the trigger.
    - `data-starting-style`: Present for the first style of its entrance: what it animates in from.
    - `data-ending-style`: Present through its exit: what it animates out to. It leaves the page when the motion ends.
- popup: The list of items. As a sheet, a design moves it by what it says of the drag, and gives it `touch-action: none` where a finger drags it.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-starting-style`: Present for the first style of its entrance: what it animates in from.
    - `data-ending-style`: Present through its exit: what it animates out to. It leaves the page when the motion ends.
    - `data-side="top | right | bottom | left | inline-start | inline-end | none"`: The side of the trigger it is on, after any flip; `none` when it lies over the trigger.
    - `data-align="start | center | end"`: How it is aligned with the anchor.
    - `data-presentation="popup | sheet"`: How the list opened: placed against its trigger, or as a sheet from the bottom edge.
    - `data-swiping`: Present while the sheet is dragged.
    - `data-swipe-dismiss`: Present once a drag has closed it.
    - `--drawer-swipe-movement-x`: As a sheet: how far it has been dragged across, always 0px.
    - `--drawer-swipe-movement-y`: As a sheet: how far it has been dragged down.
    - `--drawer-swipe-progress`: As a sheet: how far it has been dragged, of its own height: 0 to 1.
    - `--drawer-swipe-strength`: As a sheet, once let go: 0.1 to 1, the share of the design's own time it should take to come to rest.
- item: One choice in the list.
    - `data-selected`: Present on the chosen item, or on each of several.
    - `data-highlighted`: Present on the item the pointer or the keyboard is on.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.

These parts write no state attribute or CSS variable of their own: `group`, `groupLabel`, `separator`, `list`, `itemText` and `itemIndicator`.

### Separator

```
import "@kirana-ui/web/separator"
```

`<kui-separator>`: `<kui-separator>` around `kui-part="root"`. `orientation`.

Attributes of the element (each also a property, in camel case):

- `orientation` (string): Whether the line lies across (the default) or stands upright: what a screen reader is told.

Parts (`kui-part`), each with the `kui-` attributes its element is read for:

- `root`

Anatomy:

```
<kui-separator>
  root
```

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- root: The line.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: The way the line runs.

### Slider

```
import "@kirana-ui/web/slider"
```

`<kui-slider>`: `<kui-slider>` around `kui-part="root"`, a `value` (which says the value as it is written), a `control` with its `track`, `indicator` and a `thumb` for each value, in the values' order (or each with its `kui-index`). A thumb draws the hidden input a form reads. `value` and `default-value` (a range with a comma), `min`, `max`, `step`, `large-step`, `min-steps-between-values`, `thumb-alignment`, `orientation`, `disabled`, `read-only`, `name`, `form`, `locale`; it tells `value-change` and `value-committed`.

Attributes of the element (each also a property, in camel case):

- `value` (string): The value, when the caller holds it: a number, or a list of numbers for a range.
- `default-value` (string): Read once. Default `min`.
- `min` (number): Default 0.
- `max` (number): Default 100.
- `step` (number): Default 1.
- `large-step` (number): What Page Up, Page Down and an arrow with Shift move by. Default 10.
- `min-steps-between-values` (number): How many steps two thumbs of a range stay apart. Default 0.
- `thumb-alignment` (string): Where a thumb is at the ends of its range. `"center"` (the default): its centre on the control's edge, so half of it lies outside. `"edge"`: its edge on the control's edge, so it stays inside. `"edge-client-only"` is the same here: nothing waits for the browser.
- `orientation` (string): Whether the track lies across (the default) or stands upright: the arrows that move a thumb follow.
- `disabled` (boolean): Disabled: it cannot be changed.
- `read-only` (boolean): Shown as it is, focusable, not changeable: no key and no pointer moves a thumb, and its value is still submitted with the form.
- `name` (string): With a name, each thumb's value is submitted with the form around the slider.
- `form` (string): The id of the form the control belongs to, when it is not inside it.
- `locale` (string): The language a value is written in; the page's by default.

Properties only:

- `format`: How a value is written.
- `getAriaValueText`: What assistive technology reads for a thumb, when the written value is not enough.

Events:

- `value-change`: `event.detail.value`, with `event.detail.details`. `preventDefault()` keeps `value` as it was.
- `value-committed`: `event.detail.value`, with `event.detail.details`. It reports something that happened: there is nothing to keep.

Parts (`kui-part`), each with the `kui-` attributes its element is read for:

- `root`
- `value`
- `control`
- `track`
- `indicator`
- `thumb`: `kui-index`

Anatomy:

```
<kui-slider>
  root
    value
    control
      track
        indicator
        thumb (repeated)
```

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- root: Groups the slider's parts.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: The way the track runs.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when it can be read but not changed.
    - `data-dragging`: Present while a pointer holds a thumb.
    - `data-touched`: Inside a Field: present once focus has left the control.
    - `data-dirty`: Inside a Field: present while the value is not the one it started with.
    - `data-filled`: Inside a Field: present while the control has a value.
    - `data-focused`: Inside a Field: present while the control has focus.
    - `data-valid`: Inside a Field: present once the value has been checked and found right.
    - `data-invalid`: Inside a Field: present while the value is wrong.
- value: The value, written.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: The way the track runs.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when it can be read but not changed.
    - `data-dragging`: Present while a pointer holds a thumb.
    - `data-touched`: Inside a Field: present once focus has left the control.
    - `data-dirty`: Inside a Field: present while the value is not the one it started with.
    - `data-filled`: Inside a Field: present while the control has a value.
    - `data-focused`: Inside a Field: present while the control has focus.
    - `data-valid`: Inside a Field: present once the value has been checked and found right.
    - `data-invalid`: Inside a Field: present while the value is wrong.
- control: What a pointer presses and drags on. It holds the track and the thumbs.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: The way the track runs.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when it can be read but not changed.
    - `data-dragging`: Present while a pointer holds a thumb.
    - `data-touched`: Inside a Field: present once focus has left the control.
    - `data-dirty`: Inside a Field: present while the value is not the one it started with.
    - `data-filled`: Inside a Field: present while the control has a value.
    - `data-focused`: Inside a Field: present while the control has focus.
    - `data-valid`: Inside a Field: present once the value has been checked and found right.
    - `data-invalid`: Inside a Field: present while the value is wrong.
- track: The whole range.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: The way the track runs.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when it can be read but not changed.
    - `data-dragging`: Present while a pointer holds a thumb.
    - `data-touched`: Inside a Field: present once focus has left the control.
    - `data-dirty`: Inside a Field: present while the value is not the one it started with.
    - `data-filled`: Inside a Field: present while the control has a value.
    - `data-focused`: Inside a Field: present while the control has focus.
    - `data-valid`: Inside a Field: present once the value has been checked and found right.
    - `data-invalid`: Inside a Field: present while the value is wrong.
- indicator: The filled part: up to the thumb, or from the first thumb to the last. Its place and length are written on it inline, and a design does not set these: `position: relative`, `inset-inline-start` and `width`, with `height: inherit` (on a vertical slider, `position: absolute`, `bottom` and `height`, with `width: inherit`).
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: The way the track runs.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when it can be read but not changed.
    - `data-dragging`: Present while a pointer holds a thumb.
    - `data-touched`: Inside a Field: present once focus has left the control.
    - `data-dirty`: Inside a Field: present while the value is not the one it started with.
    - `data-filled`: Inside a Field: present while the control has a value.
    - `data-focused`: Inside a Field: present while the control has focus.
