    - `data-valid`: Inside a Field: present once the value has been checked and found right.
    - `data-invalid`: Inside a Field: present while the value is wrong.
    - `--start-position`: With thumbs that stay inside the control: where the filled part starts, or with one thumb where it ends.
    - `--relative-size`: With thumbs that stay inside the control and a range: the filled part's length.
- thumb: What is dragged, and what the keyboard moves: a slider to assistive technology. Its place on the track is written on it inline, and a design does not set these: `position: absolute`, `inset-inline-start` at its value's place and `top: 50%` (on a vertical slider, `bottom` and `left: 50%`), and a `translate` that centres it there (with `thumbAlignment: "edge"`, one that keeps it inside). The track needs `position: relative`. It holds a hidden input, which a form reads. A thumb that is given no `index` is the value at its place among the slider's thumbs, in the order they are written.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: The way the track runs.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when it can be read but not changed.
    - `data-dragging`: Present while a pointer holds a thumb.
    - `data-touched`: Inside a Field: present once focus has left the control.
    - `data-dirty`: Inside a Field: present while the value is not the one it started with.
    - `data-filled`: Inside a Field: present while the control has a value.
    - `data-focused`: Inside a Field: present while the control has focus.
    - `data-valid`: Inside a Field: present once the value has been checked and found right.
    - `data-invalid`: Inside a Field: present while the value is wrong.
    - `data-index`: Which thumb it is, from 0.
    - `--position`: With thumbs that stay inside the control: where the thumb's centre is.

### Steps

```
import "@kirana-ui/web/steps"
```

`<kui-steps>`: `<kui-steps>` around `kui-part="root"`, a `list` with an `item` for each step (`kui-index`, from 0, or its place in the page when it has none) holding its `trigger` (with an `indicator` inside) and a `separator`, a `content` for each step (`kui-index`), a `completed`, and `previous` and `next` buttons. `step`, `default-step`, `count` (the items in the page when it is left out), `linear`, `orientation`; it tells `step-change`.

Attributes of the element (each also a property, in camel case):

- `step` (number): The step shown, from 0. Equal to `count`, every step is done.
- `default-step` (number): The step it starts at, when the caller does not hold `step`. Read once.
- `count` (number): How many steps there are. Left out, the items in the page, counted once they are there: until then (and on a server) no step is the last, so none is all done. Give it where only some of the steps are drawn.
- `linear` (boolean): In order only: a step that is not done yet cannot be gone to by its trigger.
- `orientation` (string): Whether the steps are laid out across (the default) or down: the arrows follow.

Events:

- `step-change`: `event.detail.step`, with `event.detail.details`. `preventDefault()` keeps `step` as it was.

Parts (`kui-part`), each with the `kui-` attributes its element is read for:

- `root`
- `list`
- `item`: `kui-index`
- `trigger`: `kui-index`
- `indicator`: `kui-index`
- `separator`: `kui-index`
- `content`: `kui-index`
- `completed`
- `previous`
- `next`

Anatomy:

```
<kui-steps>
  root
    list
      item (repeated)
        trigger
          indicator (optional)
        separator (optional)
    content (repeated)
    completed (optional)
    previous (optional)
    next (optional)
```

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- root: A task in steps, taken in order.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: Whether the steps are laid out across or down.
    - `data-complete`: Present once every step is done.
- list: The row of steps: the arrows move between their triggers.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: Whether the steps are laid out across or down.
- item: One step of the row, around its trigger and its separator.
    - `data-current`: Present on the step that is shown.
    - `data-complete`: Present on a step that is done: one before the step shown.
    - `data-incomplete`: Present on a step still to come.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: Whether the steps are laid out across or down.
- trigger: Names a step, and goes to it when pressed.
    - `data-current`: Present on the step that is shown.
    - `data-complete`: Present on a step that is done: one before the step shown.
    - `data-incomplete`: Present on a step still to come.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: Whether the steps are laid out across or down.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- indicator: An element hidden from assistive technology (`aria-hidden`) that holds the step's mark as the design draws it (its number, a tick once it is done) by its `data-current`, `data-complete` and `data-incomplete`. It has no content of its own.
    - `data-current`: Present on the step that is shown.
    - `data-complete`: Present on a step that is done: one before the step shown.
    - `data-incomplete`: Present on a step still to come.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: Whether the steps are laid out across or down.
- separator: The line from a step to the next.
    - `data-current`: Present on the step that is shown.
    - `data-complete`: Present on a step that is done: one before the step shown.
    - `data-incomplete`: Present on a step still to come.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: Whether the steps are laid out across or down.
- content: What a step shows: hidden unless its step is the one shown.
    - `data-current`: Present on the step that is shown.
    - `data-complete`: Present on a step that is done: one before the step shown.
    - `data-incomplete`: Present on a step still to come.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: Whether the steps are laid out across or down.
- completed: What is shown once every step is done: hidden until then.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: Whether the steps are laid out across or down.
- previous: Goes to the step before.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- next: Goes to the step after; from the last, to all of them done.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.

### Switch

```
import "@kirana-ui/web/switch"
```

`<kui-switch>`: `<kui-switch>` around a `kui-part="root"` button with a `thumb` inside. The root draws the hidden native input a form and a label reach. `checked`, `default-checked`, `disabled`, `read-only`, `required`, `name`, `form`, `value`; it tells `checked-change`.

Attributes of the element (each also a property, in camel case):

- `checked` (boolean): Whether it is checked, when the caller holds it.
- `default-checked` (boolean): Read once.
- `disabled` (boolean): Disabled: it cannot be changed.
- `read-only` (boolean): Shown as it is, focusable, not changeable.
- `required` (boolean): Needed: in a `Field`, leaving it unchecked is then invalid.
- `name` (string): With a name, the control is submitted with the form around it when it is checked.
- `form` (string): The id of the form the control belongs to, when it is not inside it.
- `value` (string): What is submitted. Default `"on"`, as a native checkbox's.
- `kui-id` (string): The id of the switch's hidden native checkbox, not of the switch: a `<label for>` names it. Inside a `Field`, that input takes the field's id instead.

Events:

- `checked-change`: `event.detail.checked`, with `event.detail.details`. `preventDefault()` keeps `checked` as it was.

Parts (`kui-part`), each with the `kui-` attributes its element is read for:

- `root`
- `thumb`

Anatomy:

```
<kui-switch>
  root
    thumb
```

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- root: The track. It holds a hidden native checkbox, which a form and a label reach.
    - `data-checked`: Present when it is checked.
    - `data-unchecked`: Present when it is not checked.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when it can be read but not changed.
    - `data-required`: Present when the form needs it.
    - `data-touched`: Inside a Field: present once focus has left the control.
    - `data-dirty`: Inside a Field: present while the value is not the one it started with.
    - `data-filled`: Inside a Field: present while the control has a value.
    - `data-focused`: Inside a Field: present while the control has focus.
    - `data-valid`: Inside a Field: present once the value has been checked and found right.
    - `data-invalid`: Inside a Field: present while the value is wrong.
- thumb: The knob that moves along the track.
    - `data-checked`: Present when it is checked.
    - `data-unchecked`: Present when it is not checked.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when it can be read but not changed.
    - `data-required`: Present when the form needs it.
    - `data-touched`: Inside a Field: present once focus has left the control.
    - `data-dirty`: Inside a Field: present while the value is not the one it started with.
    - `data-filled`: Inside a Field: present while the control has a value.
    - `data-focused`: Inside a Field: present while the control has focus.
    - `data-valid`: Inside a Field: present once the value has been checked and found right.
    - `data-invalid`: Inside a Field: present while the value is wrong.

### Tabs

```
import "@kirana-ui/web/tabs"
```

`<kui-tabs>`: `<kui-tabs>` around `kui-part="root"`, a `list` with a `tab` for each `value` and an `indicator`, and a `panel` for each `value`, in the page while its tab is the active one. `value`, `default-value`, `orientation`; it tells `value-change`.

Attributes of the element (each also a property, in camel case):

- `value` (string): The active tab's value; `null` is "none".
- `default-value` (string): Read once. Without one, the first tab that can be chosen is, once the page is there.
- `orientation` (string): Whether the tabs are laid out across (the default) or down: the arrows that move between them follow.

Events:

- `value-change`: `event.detail.value`, with `event.detail.details`. `preventDefault()` keeps `value` as it was.

Parts (`kui-part`), each with the `kui-` attributes its element is read for:

- `root`
- `list`
- `indicator`
- `tab`: `kui-disabled`, `kui-value`
- `panel`: `kui-value`

Anatomy:

```
<kui-tabs>
  root
    list
      tab (repeated)
      indicator
    panel (repeated)
```

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- root: Groups the tabs and their panels.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: The way the tabs are laid out.
    - `data-activation-direction="left | right | up | down | none"`: Where the newly active tab is from the one before, for a panel or a mark that slides.
- list: The row of tabs. The arrows move between them.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: The way the tabs are laid out.
    - `data-activation-direction="left | right | up | down | none"`: Where the newly active tab is from the one before, for a panel or a mark that slides.
- tab: A button that shows its panel.
    - `data-active`: Present on the tab whose panel is shown.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: The way the tabs are laid out.
    - `data-activation-direction="left | right | up | down | none"`: Where the newly active tab is from the one before, for a panel or a mark that slides.
- indicator: A mark for the active tab: it carries that tab's position and size.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: The way the tabs are laid out.
    - `data-activation-direction="left | right | up | down | none"`: Where the newly active tab is from the one before, for a panel or a mark that slides.
    - `--active-tab-left`: The active tab's distance from the list's left edge.
    - `--active-tab-right`: The active tab's distance from the list's right edge.
    - `--active-tab-top`: The active tab's distance from the list's top edge.
    - `--active-tab-bottom`: The active tab's distance from the list's bottom edge.
    - `--active-tab-width`: The active tab's width.
    - `--active-tab-height`: The active tab's height.
- panel: A tab's content. In the page while its tab is active, and through its exit.
    - `data-hidden`: Present while its tab is not the active one.
    - `data-index`: The panel's place among the panels in the page, from 0, once it is in the page.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: The way the tabs are laid out.
    - `data-activation-direction="left | right | up | down | none"`: Where the newly active tab is from the one before, for a panel or a mark that slides.
    - `data-starting-style`: Present for the first style of its entrance: what it animates in from.
    - `data-ending-style`: Present through its exit: what it animates out to. It leaves the page when the motion ends.

### TagsInput

```
import "@kirana-ui/web/tags-input"
```

`<kui-tags-input>`: `<kui-tags-input>` around `kui-part="root"`, which holds a `list` with a `<template kui-each="items">` for a tag (`{value}` is its text, `{index}` its place): an `item` holding its `item-text`, which says the tag unless the page wrote something, and optionally an `item-input` to edit it in place and an `item-remove` button. Beside the list, the `input` a new tag is typed in and a `clear` button. The root draws the hidden inputs a form reads, as its last children. `value` and `default-value` (with commas between), `max`, `allow-duplicates`, `delimiter`, `add-on-blur`, `add-on-paste`, `editable`, `disabled`, `read-only`, `required`, `name`, `form`; `validate`, and `delimiter` when it is a pattern, as properties. It tells `value-change`, and `value-invalid` (`detail.text`, `detail.reason`) for a text that was not made a tag.

Attributes of the element (each also a property, in camel case):

- `value` (string): The tags, in order.
- `default-value` (string): The tags it starts with, when the caller does not hold `value`. Read once.
- `max` (number): How many tags it holds at most.
- `allow-duplicates` (boolean): Whether the same text may be a tag twice. Default `false`.
- `delimiter` (string): What ends a tag as it is typed or pasted, beside Enter. Default `","`. `null` for nothing.
- `add-on-blur` (boolean): Whether what is typed becomes a tag as focus leaves the input. Default `false`.
- `add-on-paste` (boolean): Whether a pasted text is cut into tags at its delimiters and line ends. Default `true`.
- `editable` (boolean): Whether a tag can be edited in place, by two presses or Enter on it. Default `true`.
- `disabled` (boolean): Disabled: nothing can be added or taken away.
- `read-only` (boolean): Shown as they are, focusable, not changeable.
- `required` (boolean): Needed: in a `Field`, holding none is then invalid.
- `name` (string): With a name, each tag is submitted under it with the form around them.
- `form` (string): The id of the form the control belongs to, when it is not inside it.

Properties only:

- `validate`: Whether a text may be a tag. Asked after the text is trimmed, and not for an empty one.

Events:

- `value-change`: `event.detail.value`, with `event.detail.details`. `preventDefault()` keeps `value` as it was.

Parts (`kui-part`), each with the `kui-` attributes its element is read for:

- `root`
- `list`
- `item`
- `item-text`
- `item-input`
- `item-remove`
- `input`
- `clear`

Lists (`<template kui-each="…">`): `items`.

Anatomy:

```
<kui-tags-input>
  root
    list
      <template kui-each="items">
        item (repeated)
          item-text
          item-input (optional)
          item-remove (optional)
    input
    clear (optional)
```

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- root: Several short texts held as tags, and the input a new one is typed in. It holds the hidden inputs a form reads.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when the tags are shown and cannot be changed.
    - `data-required`: Present when a tag is needed.
    - `data-focused`: Present while focus is on a tag or in the input.
    - `data-empty`: Present while it holds no tag.
- list: What holds the tags: a list.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when the tags are shown and cannot be changed.
    - `data-required`: Present when a tag is needed.
- item: A tag: reached with the arrows, taken away with Backspace or Delete.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when the tags are shown and cannot be changed.
    - `data-required`: Present when a tag is needed.
    - `data-editing`: Present while the tag is edited.
- itemText: A tag's text: hidden while the tag is edited.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when the tags are shown and cannot be changed.
    - `data-required`: Present when a tag is needed.
- itemInput: Where a tag is edited in place: hidden unless it is being edited.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when the tags are shown and cannot be changed.
    - `data-required`: Present when a tag is needed.
- itemRemove: A tag's button that takes it away.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when the tags are shown and cannot be changed.
    - `data-required`: Present when a tag is needed.
- input: Where a new tag is typed. In a `Field` it is what the field's label names; an `id` given to it is kept, so a `<label for>` names it outside one.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when the tags are shown and cannot be changed.
    - `data-required`: Present when a tag is needed.
- clear: Takes every tag away: hidden while there is none.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when the tags are shown and cannot be changed.
    - `data-required`: Present when a tag is needed.

### TimeField

```
import "@kirana-ui/web/time-field"
```

`<kui-time-field>`: `<kui-time-field>` around `kui-part="root"`, which holds a `<template kui-each="segments">` with the `segment` each part of the time is typed in (`{type}` and `{index}` say which), and the hidden `input` a form reads. `value`, `default-value`, `granularity`, `hour-cycle`, `locale`, `min`, `max`, `disabled`, `read-only`, `required`, `name`, `form`; `placeholders` as a property; it tells `value-change`. Inside a `<kui-field>` it is the field's control.

Attributes of the element (each also a property, in camel case):

- `value` (string): The time typed, once all of it is; `null` until then.
- `default-value` (string): The value it starts with, when the caller does not hold `value`. Read once.
- `granularity` (string): To the minute (`HH:MM`, the default) or to the second (`HH:MM:SS`).
- `hour-cycle` (number): A clock of 12 or 24 hours, whatever the locale's is.
- `locale` (string): The language and region that order the parts, put what stands between them and say whether the clock has twelve hours or twenty-four (`"en-US"`: 12, with AM and PM). Give it: a server does not know the reader's.
- `min` (string): The first time it takes: before it, it says it is invalid.
- `max` (string): The last time it takes.
- `disabled` (boolean): Disabled: it cannot be changed.
- `read-only` (boolean): Shown as it is, focusable, not changeable.
- `required` (boolean): Needed: in a `Field`, leaving it empty is then invalid.
- `name` (string): The name it is submitted under, by its hidden input; in a `Field`, the field's by default.
- `form` (string): The id of the form it belongs to, when it is not inside it.

Properties only:

- `placeholders`: What an empty part shows. Default: `hh`, `mm`, `ss`, and `--` for the day period.

Events:

- `value-change`: `event.detail.value`, with `event.detail.details`. `preventDefault()` keeps `value` as it was.

Parts (`kui-part`), each with the `kui-` attributes its element is read for:

- `root`
- `segment`
- `input`

Lists (`<template kui-each="…">`): `segments`.

Anatomy:

```
<kui-time-field>
  root
    <template kui-each="segments">
      segment (repeated)
    input
```

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- root: The field: a group of the time's parts. Inside a `Field` it is the field's control: the field's label names it (a press on the label goes to its first empty part), its description and messages describe it, and the field checks it.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when its value cannot be changed.
    - `data-invalid`: Present when the time is outside what it takes, is asked for and half typed, or is wrong by its field.
    - `data-touched`: In a field: present once focus has left it.
    - `data-dirty`: In a field: present while the time is not the one it began with.
    - `data-filled`: In a field: present while it holds a time.
    - `data-focused`: In a field: present while one of its parts has focus.
    - `data-valid`: In a field: present once the time was checked and found right.
- segment: One piece of the time: a part that is typed, or what stands between two.
    - `data-segment="hour | minute | second | dayPeriod | literal"`: Which piece it is: `dayPeriod` is AM or PM, on a clock of twelve hours.
    - `data-placeholder`: Present on a part that is empty.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-invalid`: Present when the time is outside what it takes, is asked for and half typed, or is wrong by its field.
    - `data-touched`: In a field: present once focus has left it.
    - `data-dirty`: In a field: present while the time is not the one it began with.
    - `data-filled`: In a field: present while it holds a time.
    - `data-focused`: In a field: present while one of its parts has focus.
    - `data-valid`: In a field: present once the time was checked and found right.

This part writes no state attribute or CSS variable of its own: `input`.

### Toast

```
import "@kirana-ui/web/toast"
```

`<kui-toast>`: `<kui-toast>` around a `kui-part="viewport"`, which holds a `<template kui-each="toasts">` with a `toast` for each message (`{id}`, `{type}`), its `content` with a `title` and a `description`, and a `close` and an `action` button. A `title`, a `description` and an `action` written empty say what the toast was added with, and are in the page only for a toast that has one; one written with something in it (`{title}`) is always there. `label`, `hotkey`, `swipe-direction`; `timeout` and `limit` for the toaster it makes, or `toaster` as a property for one of the page's own. A title, a description and an action's label are strings.

Attributes of the element (each also a property, in camel case):

- `label` (string)
- `hotkey` (string)
- `swipe-direction` (string)
- `timeout` (number)
- `limit` (number)

Properties only:

- `toaster`

Parts (`kui-part`), each with the `kui-` attributes its element is read for:

- `viewport`
- `toast`
- `content`
- `title`
- `description`
- `close`
- `action`

Lists (`<template kui-each="…">`): `toasts`.

Anatomy:

```
<kui-toast>
  viewport
    <template kui-each="toasts">
      toast (repeated)
        content (optional)
          title
          description
        close
        action
```

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- viewport: Where the toasts are drawn: a region that is always in the page.
    - `data-expanded`: Present while the pointer or focus is on the stack: the toasts are spread out, and wait.
    - `--toast-frontmost-height`: The height of the newest toast.
- root: One toast.
    - `data-starting-style`: Present for the first style of its entrance: what it animates in from.
    - `data-ending-style`: Present through its exit: what it animates out to. It leaves the page when the motion ends.
    - `data-expanded`: Present while the pointer or focus is on the stack: the toasts are spread out, and wait.
    - `data-type`: The kind the toast was added as.
    - `data-limited`: Present on a toast behind as many as are shown at once.
    - `data-swiping`: Present while the toast is dragged.
    - `data-swipe-direction="left | right | up | down"`: The way the toast was dragged out, once it has been.
    - `--toast-index`: Its place in the stack: 0 for the newest.
    - `--toast-height`: Its height.
    - `--toast-offset-y`: The height of the toasts in front of it.
    - `--toast-swipe-movement-x`: How far it has been dragged across.
    - `--toast-swipe-movement-y`: How far it has been dragged up or down.
- content: What holds a toast's contents, when the design sizes the toast itself.
    - `data-behind`: Present on a toast that is behind the newest.
    - `data-expanded`: Present while the pointer or focus is on the stack: the toasts are spread out, and wait.
- title: What the toast is called: the title it was added with, when nothing else is written in it.
    - `data-type`: The kind the toast was added as.
- description: What the toast says: the description it was added with, when nothing else is written in it.
    - `data-type`: The kind the toast was added as.
- close: Closes the toast.
    - `data-type`: The kind the toast was added as.
- action: A button of the toast's own: the action it was added with, when nothing else is written in it. Pressing it closes the toast too, unless the action refuses.
    - `data-type`: The kind the toast was added as.

### Toggle

```
import "@kirana-ui/web/toggle"
```

`<kui-toggle>`: `<kui-toggle>` around a `kui-part="root"` button. Inside a `<kui-toggle-group>` it is one of the group's, by its `value`; inside a `<kui-toolbar>`, one of its items. `pressed`, `default-pressed`, `disabled`, `value`; it tells `pressed-change`.

Attributes of the element (each also a property, in camel case):

- `pressed` (boolean): Whether it is pressed, when the caller holds it.
- `default-pressed` (boolean): Read once.
- `disabled` (boolean): Disabled: a press does nothing.
- `value` (string): In a toggle group: what the group's value holds while this one is pressed.

Events:

- `pressed-change`: `event.detail.pressed`, with `event.detail.details`. `preventDefault()` keeps `pressed` as it was.

Parts (`kui-part`), each with the `kui-` attributes its element is read for:

- `root`

Anatomy:

```
<kui-toggle>
  root
```

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- root: The button. It stays pressed until it is pressed again.
    - `data-pressed`: Present while it is pressed.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.

### ToggleGroup

```
import "@kirana-ui/web/toggle-group"
```

`<kui-toggle-group>`: `<kui-toggle-group>` around `kui-part="root"` and its `<kui-toggle>`s, each with a `value`. `value` and `default-value` (the pressed ones, with commas between), `multiple`, `disabled`, `orientation`, `loop-focus`; it tells `value-change`.

Attributes of the element (each also a property, in camel case):

- `value` (string): The values of the pressed toggles: none, one, or with `multiple` several.
- `default-value` (string): The values pressed at the start, when the caller does not hold `value`. Read once.
- `multiple` (boolean): Whether more than one can be pressed at a time.
- `disabled` (boolean): Disables every toggle of the group.
- `orientation` (string): Whether the toggles are laid out across (the default) or down: the arrows that move between them follow.
- `loop-focus` (boolean): Whether the arrows go round from the last toggle to the first. Default: they do.

Events:

- `value-change`: `event.detail.value`, with `event.detail.details`. `preventDefault()` keeps `value` as it was.

Parts (`kui-part`), each with the `kui-` attributes its element is read for:

- `root`

Anatomy:

```
<kui-toggle-group>
  root
```

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- root: The group. A toggle inside it with a `value` is one of its toggles.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: Whether its toggles are in a row or a column.
    - `data-multiple`: Present when several can be pressed at a time.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.

### Toolbar

```
import "@kirana-ui/web/toolbar"
```

`<kui-toolbar>`

Attributes of the element (each also a property, in camel case):

- `orientation` (string): Whether the controls are laid out across (the default) or down: the arrows that move between them follow.
- `loop-focus` (boolean): Whether the arrows go round from the last item to the first. Default: they do.
- `disabled` (boolean): Disables every control of the toolbar.

Parts (`kui-part`), each with the `kui-` attributes its element is read for:

- `root`
- `button`: `kui-disabled`, `kui-focusable-when-disabled`, `kui-label`
- `input`: `kui-disabled`, `kui-focusable-when-disabled`, `kui-label`
- `group`: `kui-disabled`, `kui-label`
- `link`
- `separator`

Anatomy:

```
<kui-toolbar>
  root
    group (optional, repeated)
      button (repeated)
      link (repeated)
      input (repeated)
    separator (repeated)
```

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- root: The toolbar. It is one stop for Tab.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: Whether the toolbar is a row or a column.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- button: A button of the toolbar.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: Whether the toolbar is a row or a column.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-focusable`: Present when it stays focusable while disabled: the arrows still reach it.
- link: A link of the toolbar.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: Whether the toolbar is a row or a column.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- input: A text input of the toolbar. The arrows are its own until the caret is at an end.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: Whether the toolbar is a row or a column.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-focusable`: Present when it stays focusable while disabled: the arrows still reach it.
- group: Items that belong together.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: Whether the toolbar is a row or a column.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- separator: A line between items, across the toolbar.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: Whether the toolbar is a row or a column.

### Tooltip

```
import "@kirana-ui/web/tooltip"
```

`<kui-tooltip>`: `<kui-tooltip>` around a `kui-part="trigger"` and a `portal` with a `positioner` (its `kui-side` and the like) around the `popup`, which may hold an `arrow`. `open`, `default-open`, `delay`, `close-delay`, `disabled`; it tells `open-change`.

Attributes of the element (each also a property, in camel case):

- `open` (boolean): Whether it is open, when the caller holds it.
- `default-open` (boolean): Whether it starts open, when the caller does not hold `open`. Read once.
- `delay` (number): How long the pointer rests on the trigger before the popup opens, in milliseconds.
- `close-delay` (number): How long after the pointer leaves the popup closes, in milliseconds.
- `disabled` (boolean): Disabled: the pointer and focus do not open it.

Events:

- `open-change`: `event.detail.open`, with `event.detail.details`. `preventDefault()` keeps `open` as it was.

Parts (`kui-part`), each with the `kui-` attributes its element is read for:

- `trigger`: `kui-close-delay`, `kui-delay`
- `positioner`: `kui-align`, `kui-align-offset`, `kui-anchor`, `kui-arrow-padding`, `kui-collision-boundary`, `kui-collision-padding`, `kui-position-method`, `kui-side`, `kui-side-offset`, `kui-sticky`
- `popup`
- `arrow`

Anatomy:

```
<kui-tooltip>
  trigger
  portal
    positioner
      popup
        arrow
```

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- trigger: The element the tooltip describes.
    - `data-popup-open`: Present when the tooltip is open.
    - `data-trigger-disabled`: Present when the tooltip is disabled: the pointer and focus on the trigger do not open it.
- positioner: Places the popup against the trigger. It carries the geometry.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-side="top | right | bottom | left | inline-start | inline-end"`: The side of the anchor it is on, after any flip. Asked for as `inline-start` or `inline-end`, it says one of those two when it is beside its anchor.
    - `data-align="start | center | end"`: How it is aligned with the anchor.
    - `data-anchor-hidden`: Present while the anchor is out of view: scrolled away, or clipped by a box around it.
    - `--anchor-width`: The anchor's width.
    - `--anchor-height`: The anchor's height.
    - `--available-width`: The width between the anchor and the edge of the viewport.
    - `--available-height`: The height between the anchor and the edge of the viewport.
    - `--transform-origin`: The point of the popup nearest its anchor, to scale from.
    - `--positioner-width`: The popup's width, as its content lays it out: a design gives the positioner `width: var(--positioner-width)` to animate a change of size.
    - `--positioner-height`: The popup's height, as its content lays it out: a design gives the positioner `height: var(--positioner-height)` to animate a change of size.
- popup: The tooltip itself.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-starting-style`: Present for the first style of its entrance: what it animates in from.
    - `data-ending-style`: Present through its exit: what it animates out to. It leaves the page when the motion ends.
    - `data-side="top | right | bottom | left | inline-start | inline-end"`: The side of the anchor it is on, after any flip. Asked for as `inline-start` or `inline-end`, it says one of those two when it is beside its anchor.
    - `data-align="start | center | end"`: How it is aligned with the anchor.
    - `data-instant="delay | focus | dismiss"`: Present when it opened or closed without its usual wait, for a design that skips the motion then.
- arrow: An element that points at the trigger, placed along the popup's edge.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-side="top | right | bottom | left | inline-start | inline-end"`: The side of the anchor it is on, after any flip. Asked for as `inline-start` or `inline-end`, it says one of those two when it is beside its anchor.
    - `data-align="start | center | end"`: How it is aligned with the anchor.
    - `data-instant="delay | focus | dismiss"`: Present when it opened or closed without its usual wait, for a design that skips the motion then.
    - `data-uncentered`: Present when the popup was pushed along its edge, so the arrow is not at the trigger's centre.

### Tour

```
import "@kirana-ui/web/tour"
```

`<kui-tour>`: `<kui-tour>` around a `kui-part="portal"`, drawn at the end of the page while a step is shown, which holds a `spotlight` and a `positioner` (`kui-side`, `kui-align`, `kui-side-offset` and the like) around the `popup`, with an `arrow`, a `title`, a `description`, and `previous`, `next` and `close` buttons. What a step says is the page's to write: its `controller` has the step shown (`shown`), its place (`current`) and how many there are (`total`). `steps` as a property; `open`, `default-open`, `step`, `default-step`, `wait-for-target`, `spotlight-padding`, `close-on-outside-press`, `interactive`, `keyboard-navigation`; it tells `open-change` and `step-change`.

Attributes of the element (each also a property, in camel case):

- `open` (boolean): Whether it is open, when the caller holds it.
- `default-open` (boolean): Whether it starts open, when the caller does not hold `open`. Read once.
- `step` (number): The index of the step shown, from 0, when the caller holds it.
- `default-step` (number): The step it starts at, when the caller does not hold `step`. Read once. Default 0.
- `wait-for-target` (number): How long a step whose target is not in the page waits for it, in milliseconds, before it is shown in the middle of the viewport. Default 1000.
- `spotlight-padding` (number): The room between the target and the edge of the spotlight's hole, in pixels. Default 4.
- `close-on-outside-press` (boolean): Whether a press on the dimmed page ends the tour. Default `false`.
- `interactive` (boolean): Whether the target can be used while its step is shown: pressed, focused, typed in. Default `false`: the target is seen, not used, and the rest of the page is inert either way.
- `keyboard-navigation` (boolean): Whether ArrowRight and ArrowLeft go on and back a step. Default `true`.

Properties only:

- `steps`: The steps, in order: each a `TourStep` (an `id`, and a `target`, `side` and `align` where it has them) with whatever else the page draws it from, such as `[{ id: "search", target: "#search", title: "Find anything" }]`.

Events:

- `open-change`: `event.detail.open`, with `event.detail.details`. `preventDefault()` keeps `open` as it was.
- `step-change`: `event.detail.step`, with `event.detail.details`. `preventDefault()` keeps `step` as it was.

Parts (`kui-part`), each with the `kui-` attributes its element is read for:

- `spotlight`
- `positioner`: `kui-align`, `kui-align-offset`, `kui-anchor`, `kui-arrow-padding`, `kui-collision-boundary`, `kui-collision-padding`, `kui-position-method`, `kui-side`, `kui-side-offset`, `kui-sticky`
- `popup`
- `arrow`
- `title`
- `description`
- `previous`
- `next`
- `close`

Anatomy:

```
<kui-tour>
  portal
    spotlight
    positioner
      popup
        arrow
        title
        description
        previous
        next
        close
```

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- spotlight: A layer over the page with a hole over the step's target, which the design draws from its variables (a clip path, or a box with a large shadow). A press on it is a press outside the tour. While the target can be used (`interactive`), presses go through it.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-starting-style`: Present for the first style of its entrance: what it animates in from.
    - `data-ending-style`: Present through its exit: what it animates out to. It leaves the page when the motion ends.
    - `data-centered`: Present while the step shown has no target in the page: the popup stands in the middle of the viewport.
    - `--spotlight-left`: The hole's left edge, from the spotlight's own left edge: the target's, less `spotlightPadding`.
    - `--spotlight-top`: The hole's top edge, from the spotlight's own top edge: the target's, less `spotlightPadding`.
    - `--spotlight-width`: The hole's width: the target's, with `spotlightPadding` on each side.
    - `--spotlight-height`: The hole's height: the target's, with `spotlightPadding` on each side. With no target, the hole is a point in the middle.
- positioner: Places the popup against the step's target, or in the middle of the viewport for a step with none. It carries the geometry.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-side="top | right | bottom | left | inline-start | inline-end"`: The side of the anchor it is on, after any flip. Asked for as `inline-start` or `inline-end`, it says one of those two when it is beside its anchor.
    - `data-align="start | center | end"`: How it is aligned with the anchor.
    - `data-centered`: Present while the step shown has no target in the page: the popup stands in the middle of the viewport.
    - `data-anchor-hidden`: Present while the anchor is out of view: scrolled away, or clipped by a box around it.
    - `--anchor-width`: The anchor's width.
    - `--anchor-height`: The anchor's height.
    - `--available-width`: The width between the anchor and the edge of the viewport.
    - `--available-height`: The height between the anchor and the edge of the viewport.
    - `--transform-origin`: The point of the popup nearest its anchor, to scale from.
- popup: The step itself: a dialog that stays in the page from the first step to the last, and moves.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-starting-style`: Present for the first style of its entrance: what it animates in from.
    - `data-ending-style`: Present through its exit: what it animates out to. It leaves the page when the motion ends.
    - `data-side="top | right | bottom | left | inline-start | inline-end"`: The side of the anchor it is on, after any flip. Asked for as `inline-start` or `inline-end`, it says one of those two when it is beside its anchor.
    - `data-align="start | center | end"`: How it is aligned with the anchor.
    - `data-centered`: Present while the step shown has no target in the page: the popup stands in the middle of the viewport.
- arrow: An element that points at the target, placed along the popup's edge.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-side="top | right | bottom | left | inline-start | inline-end"`: The side of the anchor it is on, after any flip. Asked for as `inline-start` or `inline-end`, it says one of those two when it is beside its anchor.
    - `data-align="start | center | end"`: How it is aligned with the anchor.
    - `data-uncentered`: Present when the popup was pushed along its edge, so the arrow is not at the target's centre.
    - `data-centered`: Present while the step shown has no target in the page: the popup stands in the middle of the viewport.
- previous: A button that goes back a step. On the first step it does nothing.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- next: A button that goes on a step. On the last step it finishes the tour.
    - `data-last`: Present on the last step: a press finishes the tour.

These parts write no state attribute or CSS variable of their own: `title`, `description` and `close`.

### Tree

```
import "@kirana-ui/web/tree"
```

`<kui-tree>`: `<kui-tree>` around `kui-part="root"` and its nodes: each an `item` (`kui-value`, and `kui-branch`, `kui-disabled`, `kui-loading`, `kui-label` as it needs), nested as the page nests them, holding an `item-row` with an `item-indicator` and an `item-text`, and, for a branch, a `group` of its children, in the page while the branch is open (`kui-keep-mounted` keeps it). A node's depth is read from the nodes around it. `expanded-value`, `default-expanded-value`, `selected-value` and `default-selected-value` (with commas between), `selection-mode`, `expand-on-click`; it tells `expanded-change` and `selected-change`.

Attributes of the element (each also a property, in camel case):

- `expanded-value` (string): The values of the open branches.
- `default-expanded-value` (string): The branches open at first, when the caller does not hold `expandedValue`. Read once.
- `selected-value` (string): The values of the chosen nodes.
- `default-selected-value` (string): The nodes chosen at first, when the caller does not hold `selectedValue`. Read once.
- `selection-mode` (string): Whether nodes can be chosen: none, one, or several. Default `single`.
- `expand-on-click` (boolean): Whether a press on a branch (or Enter on it) also opens or closes it. Default `true`.

Events:

- `expanded-change`: `event.detail.expandedValue`, with `event.detail.details`. `preventDefault()` keeps `expandedValue` as it was.
- `selected-change`: `event.detail.selectedValue`, with `event.detail.details`. `preventDefault()` keeps `selectedValue` as it was.

Parts (`kui-part`), each with the `kui-` attributes its element is read for:

- `root`
- `item`: `kui-branch`, `kui-disabled`, `kui-label`, `kui-loading`, `kui-part`, `kui-value`
- `item-row`: `kui-branch`, `kui-disabled`, `kui-label`, `kui-loading`, `kui-part`, `kui-value`
- `item-indicator`: `kui-branch`, `kui-disabled`, `kui-label`, `kui-loading`, `kui-part`, `kui-value`
- `item-text`: `kui-branch`, `kui-disabled`, `kui-label`, `kui-loading`, `kui-part`, `kui-value`
- `group`: `kui-branch`, `kui-disabled`, `kui-label`, `kui-loading`, `kui-part`, `kui-value`

Anatomy:

```
<kui-tree>
  root
    item (repeated)
      item-row (optional)
        item-indicator
        item-text
      group
        item (repeated, as above)
```

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- item: One node, a `treeitem`: a leaf, or a branch that holds its row and its group. Its `value` tells it from the others; its depth, and its place among its siblings, are read from the page.
    - `data-selected`: Present on a chosen node.
    - `data-highlighted`: Present on the node focus is on, while it is in the tree.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-open`: Present on a branch that is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present on a branch that is closed.
    - `data-loading`: Present on a branch that says its children are being loaded.
- itemRow: The line a node draws, apart from the children its group holds: what a design gives a background.
    - `data-selected`: Present on a chosen node.
    - `data-highlighted`: Present on the node focus is on, while it is in the tree.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-open`: Present on a branch that is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present on a branch that is closed.
    - `data-loading`: Present on a branch that says its children are being loaded.
- itemIndicator: The mark that says whether a branch is open. A press on it opens or closes the branch and chooses nothing.
    - `data-open`: Present on a branch that is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present on a branch that is closed.
    - `data-loading`: Present on a branch that says its children are being loaded.
- group: A branch's children. In the page while the branch is open, and through its exit's motion.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-starting-style`: Present for the first style of its entrance: what it animates in from.
    - `data-ending-style`: Present through its exit: what it animates out to. It leaves the page when the motion ends.
    - `--tree-group-height`: The group's content height while it opens or closes, `auto` once it is open.
    - `--tree-group-width`: The group's content width while it opens or closes, `auto` once it is open.

These parts write no state attribute or CSS variable of their own: `root` and `itemText`.
